42	## Sealed comparison (U57, U58)
43	- Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 and s15. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, or from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs. Criteria, margins, reference values and thresholds are fixed by a science step before the run and hidden from the run's agents. Compute is recorded per invocation and covers the arm's own subprocess only. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged.
44	- Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, replicates, warmup, order_seed, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, comparisons}`:
45	  - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual.
46	  - `inputs`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{id, spec}`: `id` a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; `spec` any JSON value (pins, case, configuration).
47	  - `outputs`: 0 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, what, format}`: a logical result each arm writes for an input, compared across arms. `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `what` a non-empty string; `format` `"bytes"`, `"text_numbers"` (every number in the file's UTF-8 text, in order, as matched by `[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?` together with `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` tokens) or `"json_numbers"` (every number leaf of the JSON document, in document order; booleans are not numbers).
48	  - `metrics`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, unit, what, source}`: `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `unit` and `what` non-empty strings; `source` `"trusted_wall"` (the wall seconds of the arm's own subprocess) or `"sealed_extraction"` (read from the arm's output by a rule the harness agent fixes before the run).
49	  - `replicates` an integer from 1 to 30; `warmup` an integer from 0 to 3; `order_seed` and `bootstrap_seed` integers; `budget_s` a positive integer, the evaluate stage's time budget for this comparison. When `args.run_ceiling_s` is present, `budget_s` must be below it.
50	  - `comparisons`: 1 to 12 items, each exactly `{id, arm, against, measure, criterion, direction, unit, pairing, rule, confidence, margin, threshold, reference, parts}`:
51	    - `id` unique, matching `^K[0-9]{1,2}$`; `arm` an arm id; `against` a different arm id or `"reference"`; `parts` a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings.
52	    - `measure` is exactly `{metric}` (a metric name) or exactly `{output, comparator}` (an output name and one of `"exact"`, `"elementwise_abs"`, `"elementwise_rel"`, `"elementwise_abs_plus_rel"`). An output comparison needs an arm as `against`.
53	    - `criterion` `"equivalence"`, `"non_inferiority"`, `"superiority"`, `"ratio_at_least"` or `"agreement"`. `agreement` is the criterion of every output comparison and of no metric comparison.
54	    - `direction` `"higher_better"`, `"lower_better"` or `"two_sided"`: the metric as measured (for wall seconds, `lower_better`). `equivalence` and `agreement` use `two_sided`; `non_inferiority` and `ratio_at_least` use `higher_better` or `lower_better`; `superiority` takes any.
55	    - `unit` `"pooled_mean"` (each replicate's value is the mean over inputs, decided once), `"per_input_all"` (decided per input; the comparison holds only if it holds on every input) or `"per_input_each"` (decided and reported per input). `ratio_at_least` uses `pooled_mean`.
56	    - `pairing` `"paired_replicate"` or `"unpaired"`; output comparisons use `paired_replicate`.
57	    - `rule` `"all_pairs"` or `"bootstrap"`; `confidence` a number in `[0.5, 1)` for `bootstrap` and null for `all_pairs`. Output comparisons use `all_pairs`.
58	    - `margin`: null, `{"abs": x}`, `{"rel": y}` or `{"abs": x, "rel": y}` with `x` and `y` finite and nonnegative. For an output comparison it is the comparator's tolerance: `elementwise_abs` needs `abs`, `elementwise_rel` needs `rel`, `elementwise_abs_plus_rel` needs both, `exact` needs null. For a metric comparison it is null, `abs` or `rel`; `rel` scales by `abs(reference)` against a reference, else by `abs(mean of the against arm's values)` for the same unit.
59	    - `threshold`: a finite number above 0 for `ratio_at_least`, otherwise null.
60	    - `reference`: exactly when `against` is `"reference"`, an object `{source, values}`: `source` a non-empty string naming where the values come from (for example an earlier run of this route), `values` mapping every input id to a finite number; otherwise null.
61	  An invalid argument or design, or a path that cannot be read as JSON, fails intake with `error_class: parse` before any agent call.
62	- Before the intake agent call and any box command, the pipeline writes atomically, in this order: `C/comparison.json`, exactly `{source, source_sha256, design}`; `C/comparison_seal.json`, exactly `{comparison_sha256, sealed_utc}` (the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of `C/comparison.json`); and `A/comparison_view.json`, exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, replicates, warmup}` copied from the design. The view holds no comparison, criterion, margin, threshold, reference value, part or budget. Agents see only the view; comparison-mode prompts name it and never `C/` or the design path. The science step that writes the design is responsible for the view's free text (`what`, `spec`) stating no expectation, criterion or result.
63	- Intake prompt, comparison mode only: the run compares the view's arms on the view's inputs; `A0` is the benchmark intake records as usual; intake also records, in `benchmark.json` under the key `arms`, each other arm's published source, pin and commands, and in `data.json` every input any arm needs.
64	- Harness prompt, comparison mode only: `setup.sh` also builds or installs every arm's published program and configuration, as published. The harness agent writes, besides the usual scripts:
65	  - one adapter `harness/arms/<arm id>.sh` per arm, `A0` included, that runs that arm's published program and configuration on the one input named by `CMP_INPUT` and writes its results under `CMP_OUT`; adapters never write or patch source, and never compute, write or assert a metric;
66	  - `harness/cmp_files.json`, exactly `{"files": {...}}`, mapping each arm id to an object that maps every output name to the relative path under `CMP_OUT` where that arm writes it;
67	  - `harness/cmp_extract.json`, exactly `{"rules": [...]}`, one rule per arm and `sealed_extraction` metric, each exactly `{arm, metric, file, kind, expr}`, with `file`, `kind` and `expr` as defined for `harness/card_extract.json` (U54) and `file` relative to `CMP_OUT`;
68	  - `harness/versions.sh`, which prints one JSON object mapping each arm id to its program's version string.
69	  Relative paths are one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none `.` or `..`. `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` keep their meaning for `A0`.
70	- After harness generation or copy (with `args.harness_from`, the source directory must also hold `arms/`, `cmp_files.json`, `cmp_extract.json` and `versions.sh`, copied like the scripts) and before the harness upload, those files must exist and be valid, and `harness/arms/` must hold exactly one non-empty adapter per arm; otherwise reproduce fails with `error_class: parse` before the upload. The pipeline then writes `C/arms_seal.json`, exactly `{files, sealed_utc}`, mapping each of those files' names (adapters as `arms/<id>.sh`) to the SHA-256 of its bytes. They upload with the harness, in the same encoding. No repair changes them.
71	- In comparison mode reproduce runs exactly as usual for `A0`. Profile, seal, propose and implement are SKIPPED. Evaluate runs the comparison when reproduce passed, and is SKIPPED otherwise, as after any failed gate.
72	- Evaluate, comparison mode (U57):
73	  - Versions: one box command, operation `versions`, runs `bash harness/versions.sh` with stdout to `out/comparison/versions.json`, then records CPU identity (`lscpu` model name and logical CPU count), the GPU driver and CUDA versions (`nvidia-smi`) and the kernel (`uname -r`) in `out/comparison/system.json`.
74	  - Rounds: `warmup` warmup rounds, then `replicates` replicate rounds. Each round runs every (arm, input) pair once, in an order drawn from one `random.Random(order_seed)` stream: one `shuffle` of the round's pairs per round, warmups included.
75	  - Each invocation is one box command, operation `comparison`, from the shared run directory. It builds a fresh `comparison-work/<round>/<arm>/<input>/` holding a symbolic link to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work`, `evaluation-work`, `units-check` and `comparison-work`, plus an empty `out/`, then runs the trusted wrapper `python3 profiler/cmp_wrap.py` (written inline by the pipeline, as the profile stage writes its probe). The wrapper runs `bash harness/arms/<arm>.sh` there and writes `out/cmp_wrap.json`, exactly `{rc, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known}`: the adapter's exit status (null on timeout), its `perf_counter` wall seconds, and GPU-busy seconds sampled while the adapter runs (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu` immediately and every second; each finite sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100` seconds, summed over GPUs; `gpu_busy_known` false when no valid sample was taken). The environment carries `CMP_ARM`, `CMP_INPUT` (the input id), `CMP_INPUT_SPEC` (the JSON of that input's `spec`), `CMP_MODE` (`warmup` or `replicate`), `CMP_ROUND` (the index) and `CMP_OUT` (the absolute path of that `out/`). The invocation's `out/` is fetched to `A/results/evaluate/comparison/<w<k> or r<k>>/<arm>/<input>/`.
76	  - Each invocation's timeout is the time left in `budget_s` (and never past the run ceiling). When it is exhausted, the remaining invocations are not run and their values are null.
77	  - Values: for an invocation that ran with `rc` 0, a `trusted_wall` metric is its `wall_s`; a `sealed_extraction` metric is its rule applied to its fetched files (a missing or unreadable file, no match or a nonfinite value gives null). Every value of an invocation with a nonzero `rc`, a timeout or a missing wrapper file is null.
78	  - Compute (G6): `A/results/evaluate/comparison_compute.json`, written atomically after the last invocation, is exactly `{invocations, arms, system, versions, box}`. `invocations` has one row per invocation in run order, each exactly `{round, arm, input, rc, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, usd}`, from the wrapper, with `usd` = `wall_s / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h` (null when the price is unavailable). `arms` has one row per arm, each exactly `{arm, invocations, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, usd}`, summed over that arm's replicate invocations. `system` and `versions` copy the fetched files (null when missing or invalid), and `box` is exactly `{type, price_usd_h}` from `C/box.json`. Uploads, links and fetches are outside every row.
79	- Scoring (U58): after the last invocation, `python3 -I m5/score_comparison.py <C dir> <A/results/evaluate/comparison dir> <A/harness dir> <C/comparison_scored.json>`. It checks the SHA-256 of `C/comparison.json` against `C/comparison_seal.json` and of each sealed harness file against `C/arms_seal.json`, then scores each comparison from the replicate rounds only.
80	  - Output comparisons (`agreement`): for each input and replicate where both arms ran with `rc` 0, the comparator reads the mapped file of each arm. `exact`: identical bytes. Otherwise both files are parsed as the output's `format` into number lists; different lengths, or a NaN in one list but not at the same position in the other, disagree; equal infinities agree; finite pairs agree when `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol` (`elementwise_abs`), `abs(a - b) <= rel_tol * abs(b)` (`elementwise_rel`, `b` the `against` arm's element) or `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * abs(b)` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel`). A pair agrees when every element agrees. Each pair records `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error` over its finite elements (null when none). A missing or unparsable file makes that pair missing.
81	  - Metric comparisons: an arm's value for (replicate, input) is the metric value above. For `pooled_mean`, a replicate's value is the mean over inputs, null when any input's value is null. The statistics are, per decision unit (the pooled value, or each input): for `paired_replicate`, the difference `arm - against` per replicate where both have values (or `arm - reference value`); for `unpaired`, the differences of every arm value with every against value (or with the reference value). `ratio_at_least` uses the ratio of means `mean(arm) / mean(against)` for `higher_better` and `mean(against) / mean(arm)` for `lower_better`, over the replicates where both have values.
82	  - Interval: for `all_pairs`, `[lo, hi]` is the minimum and maximum of the differences (for a ratio, of the per-replicate ratios in the same orientation), and needs at least one difference. For `bootstrap`, the statistic (the mean difference, or the ratio of means) is recomputed on 10000 resamples with replacement of the unit's paired replicates (for `unpaired`, of each arm's values separately), drawn from one `random.Random(bootstrap_seed)` stream in comparison order, and `[lo, hi]` is the `(1 - confidence) / 2` and `(1 + confidence) / 2` empirical quantiles (sorted resamples, index `floor(q * 9999)`); it needs at least two replicates. `estimate` is the statistic on the full data. Too few values gives outcome `"void"` with reason `"insufficient_replicates"`; no values at all gives reason `"missing_values"`.
83	  - Margin value `m`: 0 for a null margin, `x` for `{"abs": x}`, and for `{"rel": y}` `y * abs(reference value)` or `y * abs(mean of the against arm's values in the unit)`.
84	  - Outcome per decision unit, `"supported"`, `"not_supported"` or else `"inconclusive"`: agreement is supported when every pair agrees and none is missing, not supported when any pair disagrees, otherwise void with reason `"missing_values"`; equivalence is supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`, not supported when `hi < -m` or `lo > m`; non-inferiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo >= -m`, not supported when `hi < -m`; non-inferiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi <= m`, not supported when `lo > m`; superiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo > m`, not supported when `hi <= m`; superiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi < -m`, not supported when `lo >= -m`; superiority (`two_sided`) is supported when `lo > m` or `hi < -m`, not supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`; ratio is supported when `lo >= threshold`, not supported when `hi < threshold`.
85	  - A comparison's outcome: for `pooled_mean`, its one unit's outcome; for `per_input_all`, supported when every input is supported, not supported when any input is not supported, void when any input is void and none is not supported, otherwise inconclusive; for `per_input_each`, `"per_input"`, with each input's outcome in its rows.
86	  - `C/comparison_scored.json`, atomic, is exactly `{comparison_sha256, comparisons, totals}`. `comparisons` follows the design's order, each exactly `{id, arm, against, criterion, unit, outcome, rows}`; `rows` has one row per decision unit (`input` null for `pooled_mean`), each exactly `{input, n, estimate, lo, hi, margin_value, threshold, outcome, reason, pairs}`. `n` counts the differences, ratios or compared pairs; `pairs` is null for metric comparisons and, for agreement, the per-replicate rows `{replicate, agrees, max_abs_error, max_rel_error}`. Numbers are null when void; `reason` is null unless void. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons.
87	  - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`.
88	- Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode, and add optional `comparisons_total`, `comparisons_supported`, `comparisons_not_supported`, `comparisons_inconclusive` and `comparisons_void` (decision units, nonnegative integers), all null outside comparison mode, on SKIPPED/stub records and whenever the scored file was not written; records without them stay valid.
89	
90	Write `CHECK.json`: exactly `{"gaps": "G1+G3+G6", "verdict": ..., "missing": [...], "problems": [...]}`:
91	- `"verdict"`: `"sufficient"` (build as written), `"partial"` (build after the listed fixes), `"insufficient"` (this design cannot serve these gaps).
92	- `"missing"`: the ids of FINAL.json's arms (`"A0"`...) and comparisons (`"K1"`...) this contract cannot run, express or decide as FINAL.json needs, plus `"compute_facts"` when a listed compute fact is not recorded; no duplicates; empty if none.
93	- `"problems"`: codes, no duplicates, empty if none, from: `"arm_not_runnable"` (an arm cannot be run by an adapter of published code and configuration), `"metric_not_capturable"` (a metric cannot come from the adapter or the trusted wall time), `"criterion_unfit"` (a criterion's decision rule is not what the question needs), `"statistic_unfit"` (the replicate aggregation, pairing, interval rule or small-sample rule cannot decide it), `"margin_rule_unfit"` (absolute or relative margins, or their base, are wrong for a comparison), `"reference_unfit"` (a fixed reference value cannot serve), `"order_unfit"` (the interleaving, warmups or seeds are wrong), `"inputs_unfit"` (inputs per invocation, or averaging over them, are wrong), `"budget_unfit"` (the evaluate budget cannot hold the rounds), `"compute_unfit"` (the compute record is wrong or incomplete), `"leaks_or_biases"` (an agent could see criteria, margins, references or ratios, or steer an arm), `"sealing_unfit"`, `"other"`.
94	
95	Write `ASSESSMENT.md` for the owner: your judgement in prose, and for each missing item or problem the smallest fix. Write `NARROWING.md` ("No narrowing." with the reason, or what changed), `PREDICTIONS.md` ("No test; no predictions."), `predictions.json` `{"items": []}`, `outcomes.json` `{"items": []}` (s15 sealed none), and `NEXT.json` `{"action": "stop", "reason": "contract_gap"}`. CHECK.json holds no free text and no seed content.
96	
97	`status.json`: one JSON object with exactly these keys, each taking only the listed values:
98	- `"verdict"`: `"sufficient"`, `"partial"`, `"insufficient"` (as in CHECK.json)
99	- `"missing_count"`: `"none"`, `"one"`, `"two_or_more"`
100	- `"problem_count"`: `"none"`, `"one"`, `"two_or_more"`
101	- `"next_action"`: `"stop"`
102	- `"stop_reason"`: `"contract_gap"`
103	- `"narrowing"`: `"none"`, `"explicit"`
104	- `"prediction_count"`: `"none"`
105	
106	No other keys and no free text. Finish within 30 minutes.

You are the scientific agent for the blind-02 experiment of the metis repository (`/home/hal/dev/interp/metis`). The owner authorized you to read its seed and records. The operator who launches you is blind: it sees only your `status.json`, validated as fixed enum values, plus file counts and hashes. Your other files are for the owner and for the next scientific step, never for the operator. Never put seed or record content into `status.json`.

## The owner's request (2026-11-03), which binds every step
The owner's impression is that run2 exposed a limitation of m5's fixed menu, while the seed's original question remains open; check that against the run's evidence. The repo has a tree/card mechanism for exploring experiments under a fixed root question, and a measure route for calibrating the cards' assumptions. Use them to continue within this seed: find candidate experiments that address different parts of the question, and inexpensive measurements that distinguish between them; carry promising candidates through calibration. You prepare the scientific inputs, including `tree_args.json`. After each result you assess what it supports and choose the next informative test. Seal predictions before each test, preserve negative results, and make any narrowing of the question explicit. If an existing mechanism cannot express a required comparison, identify the specific contract gap (file, section, what it cannot express). Stop when there is no justified next test, the limits are reached, or the owner's input is genuinely necessary.

## Where things are (paths relative to the repo root)
- Seed and materials: `experiments/blind-02/m5/BRIEF.md` (the owner's seed, verbatim) and `experiments/blind-02/m5/b01_materials/BRIEF_run1.md` (seed plus a materials addendum copied from blind-01 records).
- m5 runs: `experiments/blind-02/m5/run1/` (intake PASS, reproduce infra failure) and `run2/` (stopped at propose, outcome no_feasible_method). Earlier readers: `m5/run2_progress2/REPORT.md`, `m5/run2_trace/REPORT.md` (a full trace of the seed's comparisons through run2; build on it rather than redo it).
- blind-01 records on the same materials, read-only, if they bear on a candidate: `experiments/blind-01/m5/` (run9 reproduce at reduced scale; run10 unit equivalence; run11 unit concurrency probe).
- Earlier science steps: `experiments/blind-02/science/sNN/` (read all earlier steps before writing).
- Tree/card: `dut/pipeline/launch.js` (kinds `tree`, `card`, `measure`), `dut/pipeline/CONTRACT.md` (question_tree_v2: section 2.5 PLAN, section 5 "Seed records" and "calibration"), `dut/pipeline/src/main.js` (args at lines 15-35; calibration records near line 468), `src/prompts.js`, `src/schemas.js`. `launch.js <exp> tree --seed <args.json>` lays your file over `experiments/question-tree/replay/args_F.json` (minus its `fixed_roots` and `base`). Keys: `seed` (integer), `fixed_roots` (root questions held fixed), `seed_ideas` (strings or option records `{title, text, root_question, kind, root_link, compute_open, sequential, source_urls}`; each becomes its own pick and card), `picks_per_branch`, `pool_k`, `require_compute_lever`, `deepen_on_signal`, `budget_usd`, `budget_covers_storage`, `budget_covers_tax`. The tree writes `experiments/blind-02/<stamp>-tree/out/result.json` with `cards`, `table`, `inventory`, `calibration[]` (state `not_judged|rejected|calibration_required|no_unmeasured_input`, `plan_usd`, `required[]` load-bearing GUESS/PROXY inputs with their measuring phase).
- Measure: `launch.js <exp> measure --card <tree run> --pick <key>` compiles one calibration record into a latent_skeptic measure folder (QUESTION.md, SEALED_PREDICTIONS.md, out/triage_args.json, CARD.json) with no model call; it checks each GUESS/PROXY input against a ratio band (2.5x PROXY, 3x otherwise) and does not carry the card's arms or decision rule (`launch.js:58-107`). The stages after it (design, gate, build, tests, review, launch, post) run via `launch.js <exp> stage --measure <dir> --stage ...` on `idea/wf.js`, but the script that wrote their args files and chained them (m4's `measure.sh`) is not available to this route; treat the measure route's execution as unproven, and say what a calibration would need from it.
- m5: `dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md`, `pipeline.js`. It can also run a calibration on a box: `~/.cache/blind01/new_run.py` options `--stop-after-reproduce` (setup and anchors only), `--stop-after-profile` (adds the profile and the concurrency probe), `--units-check=run<N>`, `--units-probe=run<N>`, `--harness-from=<dir>`.

## Limits (the operator enforces them; plan within them)
- Compute: pilot cap USD 2,000, of which about USD 126 of box time is spent. Each calibration box run must project under USD 20 (the owner's standing rule: calibration and smoke runs about USD 10 each need no re-approval; above USD 20 needs owner approval before launch). One box run: 6 h soft limit, 12 h hard ceiling. The cards' full planned experiments are not run on this route; only calibrations are.
- Inference is scarce. Prefer one tree run with few picks (`picks_per_branch` 1) over several.
- No new seed from you: work within the owner's seed. Narrowing is allowed only when stated explicitly in `NARROWING.md` (what the root question keeps, what it drops, why).

## Rules
- Read anything under `experiments/blind-02/`, `experiments/blind-01/m5/` and `dut/`. Write only into your step folder (the current directory). Never read `.keys` files, credential files or anything under `~/.codex/`. Run no git commands. Do not contact any box. Network: only if your step brief allows it.
- No fabrication. When something cannot be established from the files, say so and use the matching `unknown` value.
- Failed and negative results stay recorded as they are; never reinterpret a criterion after seeing a result.

## Files you write in your step folder
- `ASSESSMENT.md` for the owner: your answers, with file and line references and numbers quoted from the files.
- `NARROWING.md`: the exact root question(s) you hold fixed, compared with the seed's question; what is kept, what is dropped, and why. Write "No narrowing." and the reason if none.
- `PREDICTIONS.md` and `predictions.json`: your predictions for the next test's outcome, written before it runs (the operator commits them before launching it, which seals them). `predictions.json` is `{"items": [{"id": "Q1", "p": 0.0-1.0}]}`, ids `Q1`..`Q20`, each id stated in `PREDICTIONS.md` as one checkable statement with how it resolves. Empty items when the next action is `stop`.
- `outcomes.json` (every step after the first): the outcomes of the previous step's predictions, `{"items": [{"id": "Q1", "outcome": true|false|null}]}` covering every previous id (null only when it cannot be resolved), with the evidence in `ASSESSMENT.md`.
- `NEXT.json`: the next test, exactly one of
  - `{"action": "tree", "tree_args": "tree_args.json"}` (and write `tree_args.json` here)
  - `{"action": "measure", "tree_run": "<folder name under experiments/blind-02/>", "pick": "<calibration record key>"}`
  - `{"action": "m5", "brief": "<file in this folder>", "new_run_flags": ["--stop-after-profile"]}` (flags only from the m5 list above; the brief is used as the run's whole brief)
  - `{"action": "stop", "reason": "no_justified_test" | "needs_owner" | "contract_gap" | "limits"}`
- `status.json` as your step brief specifies. End with a final reply that is exactly the contents of `status.json`.

## Step s16 (content check of the revised G1/G3/G6 contract; no network; no new test)
Your step folder is `experiments/blind-02/science/s16/`. Read `science/s09/`, `science/s13/`, `science/s14/` and `science/s15/` first (REQS.json, PARTS.json, FINAL.json, SHAPES.json, ASSESSMENT.md). s14 judged the operator's first draft `partial`; s15 gave each comparison's shape and the fixes (SHAPES.json). The operator revised the draft once, from those codes alone, without reading the seed or any prose. Judge also whether every fix and shape s15 chose is met, including any `other` you or s15 described; this is the operator's one revision, so a second `partial` goes to the owner with your assessment. It is a draft for a new section of `dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md` (units U57 and U58), not yet committed, because the worktree is building U54 to U56. Judge whether it, as written, can express and decide each comparison K1..Kn of FINAL.json, run each arm, and record the compute facts FINAL.json asks for. A design file in this format would be written later by a science step, with margins fixed before the run (the owner's choice where FINAL.json says so); do not write it now. Nothing is built yet.

The contract section, verbatim:

## Sealed comparison (U57, U58)
- Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 and s15. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, or from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs. Criteria, margins, reference values and thresholds are fixed by a science step before the run and hidden from the run's agents. Compute is recorded per invocation and covers the arm's own subprocess only. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged.
- Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, replicates, warmup, order_seed, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, comparisons}`:
  - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual.
  - `inputs`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{id, spec}`: `id` a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; `spec` any JSON value (pins, case, configuration).
  - `outputs`: 0 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, what, format}`: a logical result each arm writes for an input, compared across arms. `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `what` a non-empty string; `format` `"bytes"`, `"text_numbers"` (every number in the file's UTF-8 text, in order, as matched by `[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?` together with `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` tokens) or `"json_numbers"` (every number leaf of the JSON document, in document order; booleans are not numbers).
  - `metrics`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, unit, what, source}`: `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `unit` and `what` non-empty strings; `source` `"trusted_wall"` (the wall seconds of the arm's own subprocess) or `"sealed_extraction"` (read from the arm's output by a rule the harness agent fixes before the run).
  - `replicates` an integer from 1 to 30; `warmup` an integer from 0 to 3; `order_seed` and `bootstrap_seed` integers; `budget_s` a positive integer, the evaluate stage's time budget for this comparison. When `args.run_ceiling_s` is present, `budget_s` must be below it.
  - `comparisons`: 1 to 12 items, each exactly `{id, arm, against, measure, criterion, direction, unit, pairing, rule, confidence, margin, threshold, reference, parts}`:
    - `id` unique, matching `^K[0-9]{1,2}$`; `arm` an arm id; `against` a different arm id or `"reference"`; `parts` a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings.
    - `measure` is exactly `{metric}` (a metric name) or exactly `{output, comparator}` (an output name and one of `"exact"`, `"elementwise_abs"`, `"elementwise_rel"`, `"elementwise_abs_plus_rel"`). An output comparison needs an arm as `against`.
    - `criterion` `"equivalence"`, `"non_inferiority"`, `"superiority"`, `"ratio_at_least"` or `"agreement"`. `agreement` is the criterion of every output comparison and of no metric comparison.
    - `direction` `"higher_better"`, `"lower_better"` or `"two_sided"`: the metric as measured (for wall seconds, `lower_better`). `equivalence` and `agreement` use `two_sided`; `non_inferiority` and `ratio_at_least` use `higher_better` or `lower_better`; `superiority` takes any.
    - `unit` `"pooled_mean"` (each replicate's value is the mean over inputs, decided once), `"per_input_all"` (decided per input; the comparison holds only if it holds on every input) or `"per_input_each"` (decided and reported per input). `ratio_at_least` uses `pooled_mean`.
    - `pairing` `"paired_replicate"` or `"unpaired"`; output comparisons use `paired_replicate`.
    - `rule` `"all_pairs"` or `"bootstrap"`; `confidence` a number in `[0.5, 1)` for `bootstrap` and null for `all_pairs`. Output comparisons use `all_pairs`.
    - `margin`: null, `{"abs": x}`, `{"rel": y}` or `{"abs": x, "rel": y}` with `x` and `y` finite and nonnegative. For an output comparison it is the comparator's tolerance: `elementwise_abs` needs `abs`, `elementwise_rel` needs `rel`, `elementwise_abs_plus_rel` needs both, `exact` needs null. For a metric comparison it is null, `abs` or `rel`; `rel` scales by `abs(reference)` against a reference, else by `abs(mean of the against arm's values)` for the same unit.
    - `threshold`: a finite number above 0 for `ratio_at_least`, otherwise null.
    - `reference`: exactly when `against` is `"reference"`, an object `{source, values}`: `source` a non-empty string naming where the values come from (for example an earlier run of this route), `values` mapping every input id to a finite number; otherwise null.
  An invalid argument or design, or a path that cannot be read as JSON, fails intake with `error_class: parse` before any agent call.
- Before the intake agent call and any box command, the pipeline writes atomically, in this order: `C/comparison.json`, exactly `{source, source_sha256, design}`; `C/comparison_seal.json`, exactly `{comparison_sha256, sealed_utc}` (the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of `C/comparison.json`); and `A/comparison_view.json`, exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, replicates, warmup}` copied from the design. The view holds no comparison, criterion, margin, threshold, reference value, part or budget. Agents see only the view; comparison-mode prompts name it and never `C/` or the design path. The science step that writes the design is responsible for the view's free text (`what`, `spec`) stating no expectation, criterion or result.
- Intake prompt, comparison mode only: the run compares the view's arms on the view's inputs; `A0` is the benchmark intake records as usual; intake also records, in `benchmark.json` under the key `arms`, each other arm's published source, pin and commands, and in `data.json` every input any arm needs.
- Harness prompt, comparison mode only: `setup.sh` also builds or installs every arm's published program and configuration, as published. The harness agent writes, besides the usual scripts:
  - one adapter `harness/arms/<arm id>.sh` per arm, `A0` included, that runs that arm's published program and configuration on the one input named by `CMP_INPUT` and writes its results under `CMP_OUT`; adapters never write or patch source, and never compute, write or assert a metric;
  - `harness/cmp_files.json`, exactly `{"files": {...}}`, mapping each arm id to an object that maps every output name to the relative path under `CMP_OUT` where that arm writes it;
  - `harness/cmp_extract.json`, exactly `{"rules": [...]}`, one rule per arm and `sealed_extraction` metric, each exactly `{arm, metric, file, kind, expr}`, with `file`, `kind` and `expr` as defined for `harness/card_extract.json` (U54) and `file` relative to `CMP_OUT`;
  - `harness/versions.sh`, which prints one JSON object mapping each arm id to its program's version string.
  Relative paths are one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none `.` or `..`. `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` keep their meaning for `A0`.
- After harness generation or copy (with `args.harness_from`, the source directory must also hold `arms/`, `cmp_files.json`, `cmp_extract.json` and `versions.sh`, copied like the scripts) and before the harness upload, those files must exist and be valid, and `harness/arms/` must hold exactly one non-empty adapter per arm; otherwise reproduce fails with `error_class: parse` before the upload. The pipeline then writes `C/arms_seal.json`, exactly `{files, sealed_utc}`, mapping each of those files' names (adapters as `arms/<id>.sh`) to the SHA-256 of its bytes. They upload with the harness, in the same encoding. No repair changes them.
- In comparison mode reproduce runs exactly as usual for `A0`. Profile, seal, propose and implement are SKIPPED. Evaluate runs the comparison when reproduce passed, and is SKIPPED otherwise, as after any failed gate.
- Evaluate, comparison mode (U57):
  - Versions: one box command, operation `versions`, runs `bash harness/versions.sh` with stdout to `out/comparison/versions.json`, then records CPU identity (`lscpu` model name and logical CPU count), the GPU driver and CUDA versions (`nvidia-smi`) and the kernel (`uname -r`) in `out/comparison/system.json`.
  - Rounds: `warmup` warmup rounds, then `replicates` replicate rounds. Each round runs every (arm, input) pair once, in an order drawn from one `random.Random(order_seed)` stream: one `shuffle` of the round's pairs per round, warmups included.
  - Each invocation is one box command, operation `comparison`, from the shared run directory. It builds a fresh `comparison-work/<round>/<arm>/<input>/` holding a symbolic link to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work`, `evaluation-work`, `units-check` and `comparison-work`, plus an empty `out/`, then runs the trusted wrapper `python3 profiler/cmp_wrap.py` (written inline by the pipeline, as the profile stage writes its probe). The wrapper runs `bash harness/arms/<arm>.sh` there and writes `out/cmp_wrap.json`, exactly `{rc, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known}`: the adapter's exit status (null on timeout), its `perf_counter` wall seconds, and GPU-busy seconds sampled while the adapter runs (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu` immediately and every second; each finite sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100` seconds, summed over GPUs; `gpu_busy_known` false when no valid sample was taken). The environment carries `CMP_ARM`, `CMP_INPUT` (the input id), `CMP_INPUT_SPEC` (the JSON of that input's `spec`), `CMP_MODE` (`warmup` or `replicate`), `CMP_ROUND` (the index) and `CMP_OUT` (the absolute path of that `out/`). The invocation's `out/` is fetched to `A/results/evaluate/comparison/<w<k> or r<k>>/<arm>/<input>/`.
  - Each invocation's timeout is the time left in `budget_s` (and never past the run ceiling). When it is exhausted, the remaining invocations are not run and their values are null.
  - Values: for an invocation that ran with `rc` 0, a `trusted_wall` metric is its `wall_s`; a `sealed_extraction` metric is its rule applied to its fetched files (a missing or unreadable file, no match or a nonfinite value gives null). Every value of an invocation with a nonzero `rc`, a timeout or a missing wrapper file is null.
  - Compute (G6): `A/results/evaluate/comparison_compute.json`, written atomically after the last invocation, is exactly `{invocations, arms, system, versions, box}`. `invocations` has one row per invocation in run order, each exactly `{round, arm, input, rc, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, usd}`, from the wrapper, with `usd` = `wall_s / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h` (null when the price is unavailable). `arms` has one row per arm, each exactly `{arm, invocations, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, usd}`, summed over that arm's replicate invocations. `system` and `versions` copy the fetched files (null when missing or invalid), and `box` is exactly `{type, price_usd_h}` from `C/box.json`. Uploads, links and fetches are outside every row.
- Scoring (U58): after the last invocation, `python3 -I m5/score_comparison.py <C dir> <A/results/evaluate/comparison dir> <A/harness dir> <C/comparison_scored.json>`. It checks the SHA-256 of `C/comparison.json` against `C/comparison_seal.json` and of each sealed harness file against `C/arms_seal.json`, then scores each comparison from the replicate rounds only.
  - Output comparisons (`agreement`): for each input and replicate where both arms ran with `rc` 0, the comparator reads the mapped file of each arm. `exact`: identical bytes. Otherwise both files are parsed as the output's `format` into number lists; different lengths, or a NaN in one list but not at the same position in the other, disagree; equal infinities agree; finite pairs agree when `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol` (`elementwise_abs`), `abs(a - b) <= rel_tol * abs(b)` (`elementwise_rel`, `b` the `against` arm's element) or `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * abs(b)` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel`). A pair agrees when every element agrees. Each pair records `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error` over its finite elements (null when none). A missing or unparsable file makes that pair missing.
  - Metric comparisons: an arm's value for (replicate, input) is the metric value above. For `pooled_mean`, a replicate's value is the mean over inputs, null when any input's value is null. The statistics are, per decision unit (the pooled value, or each input): for `paired_replicate`, the difference `arm - against` per replicate where both have values (or `arm - reference value`); for `unpaired`, the differences of every arm value with every against value (or with the reference value). `ratio_at_least` uses the ratio of means `mean(arm) / mean(against)` for `higher_better` and `mean(against) / mean(arm)` for `lower_better`, over the replicates where both have values.
  - Interval: for `all_pairs`, `[lo, hi]` is the minimum and maximum of the differences (for a ratio, of the per-replicate ratios in the same orientation), and needs at least one difference. For `bootstrap`, the statistic (the mean difference, or the ratio of means) is recomputed on 10000 resamples with replacement of the unit's paired replicates (for `unpaired`, of each arm's values separately), drawn from one `random.Random(bootstrap_seed)` stream in comparison order, and `[lo, hi]` is the `(1 - confidence) / 2` and `(1 + confidence) / 2` empirical quantiles (sorted resamples, index `floor(q * 9999)`); it needs at least two replicates. `estimate` is the statistic on the full data. Too few values gives outcome `"void"` with reason `"insufficient_replicates"`; no values at all gives reason `"missing_values"`.
  - Margin value `m`: 0 for a null margin, `x` for `{"abs": x}`, and for `{"rel": y}` `y * abs(reference value)` or `y * abs(mean of the against arm's values in the unit)`.
  - Outcome per decision unit, `"supported"`, `"not_supported"` or else `"inconclusive"`: agreement is supported when every pair agrees and none is missing, not supported when any pair disagrees, otherwise void with reason `"missing_values"`; equivalence is supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`, not supported when `hi < -m` or `lo > m`; non-inferiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo >= -m`, not supported when `hi < -m`; non-inferiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi <= m`, not supported when `lo > m`; superiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo > m`, not supported when `hi <= m`; superiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi < -m`, not supported when `lo >= -m`; superiority (`two_sided`) is supported when `lo > m` or `hi < -m`, not supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`; ratio is supported when `lo >= threshold`, not supported when `hi < threshold`.
  - A comparison's outcome: for `pooled_mean`, its one unit's outcome; for `per_input_all`, supported when every input is supported, not supported when any input is not supported, void when any input is void and none is not supported, otherwise inconclusive; for `per_input_each`, `"per_input"`, with each input's outcome in its rows.
  - `C/comparison_scored.json`, atomic, is exactly `{comparison_sha256, comparisons, totals}`. `comparisons` follows the design's order, each exactly `{id, arm, against, criterion, unit, outcome, rows}`; `rows` has one row per decision unit (`input` null for `pooled_mean`), each exactly `{input, n, estimate, lo, hi, margin_value, threshold, outcome, reason, pairs}`. `n` counts the differences, ratios or compared pairs; `pairs` is null for metric comparisons and, for agreement, the per-replicate rows `{replicate, agrees, max_abs_error, max_rel_error}`. Numbers are null when void; `reason` is null unless void. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons.
  - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`.
- Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode, and add optional `comparisons_total`, `comparisons_supported`, `comparisons_not_supported`, `comparisons_inconclusive` and `comparisons_void` (decision units, nonnegative integers), all null outside comparison mode, on SKIPPED/stub records and whenever the scored file was not written; records without them stay valid.

Write `CHECK.json`: exactly `{"gaps": "G1+G3+G6", "verdict": ..., "missing": [...], "problems": [...]}`:
- `"verdict"`: `"sufficient"` (build as written), `"partial"` (build after the listed fixes), `"insufficient"` (this design cannot serve these gaps).
- `"missing"`: the ids of FINAL.json's arms (`"A0"`...) and comparisons (`"K1"`...) this contract cannot run, express or decide as FINAL.json needs, plus `"compute_facts"` when a listed compute fact is not recorded; no duplicates; empty if none.
- `"problems"`: codes, no duplicates, empty if none, from: `"arm_not_runnable"` (an arm cannot be run by an adapter of published code and configuration), `"metric_not_capturable"` (a metric cannot come from the adapter or the trusted wall time), `"criterion_unfit"` (a criterion's decision rule is not what the question needs), `"statistic_unfit"` (the replicate aggregation, pairing, interval rule or small-sample rule cannot decide it), `"margin_rule_unfit"` (absolute or relative margins, or their base, are wrong for a comparison), `"reference_unfit"` (a fixed reference value cannot serve), `"order_unfit"` (the interleaving, warmups or seeds are wrong), `"inputs_unfit"` (inputs per invocation, or averaging over them, are wrong), `"budget_unfit"` (the evaluate budget cannot hold the rounds), `"compute_unfit"` (the compute record is wrong or incomplete), `"leaks_or_biases"` (an agent could see criteria, margins, references or ratios, or steer an arm), `"sealing_unfit"`, `"other"`.

Write `ASSESSMENT.md` for the owner: your judgement in prose, and for each missing item or problem the smallest fix. Write `NARROWING.md` ("No narrowing." with the reason, or what changed), `PREDICTIONS.md` ("No test; no predictions."), `predictions.json` `{"items": []}`, `outcomes.json` `{"items": []}` (s15 sealed none), and `NEXT.json` `{"action": "stop", "reason": "contract_gap"}`. CHECK.json holds no free text and no seed content.

`status.json`: one JSON object with exactly these keys, each taking only the listed values:
- `"verdict"`: `"sufficient"`, `"partial"`, `"insufficient"` (as in CHECK.json)
- `"missing_count"`: `"none"`, `"one"`, `"two_or_more"`
- `"problem_count"`: `"none"`, `"one"`, `"two_or_more"`
- `"next_action"`: `"stop"`
- `"stop_reason"`: `"contract_gap"`
- `"narrowing"`: `"none"`, `"explicit"`
- `"prediction_count"`: `"none"`

No other keys and no free text. Finish within 30 minutes.

11	## Verdict: partial (the operator's one revision; this goes to the owner)

13	The revision is a large improvement, and its structure should be kept. In particular, the trusted cross-arm comparator, one input per invocation, per-input references, the `unpaired` + `all_pairs` worst-case interval, the bootstrap ratio of means and the per-invocation compute rows each closes a gap from s14.
14	
15	Every remaining gap can be fixed by adding to the draft, and none needs a redesign. So the verdict is `partial`, not `insufficient`. Even so, none of the seven comparisons can yet be decided exactly as FINAL.json and the card seal them, and the billed-cost fact is still not recorded. One gap carries most of the weight: **the draft has no trusted evaluator**. Per-pose DockQ is behind K3, K6 and K7, and it is part of K4's timing scope. The draft gives DockQ nowhere to run, because adapters may not compute a metric and the native structures must reach only the evaluator (PC:23, 36).

18

20	|---|---|---|
21	| inputs `one_input_per_invocation` | met | Rounds: each (arm, input) pair is its own invocation, with `CMP_INPUT` |

32	| K1 shape (outputs, elementwise_abs, per_input_all, paired, all_pairs) | expressible, but see K1 | |

40	- **Gating of K4–K7 on K1–K3** (PC:65, 102). Write the agreement phase as its own design (K1–K3, A0 and A1, 1 replicate, matching "1 invocation per arm/case", PC:101). Launch the main design only if every agreement comparison is `supported`. The draft's split rule allows this.

With `unpaired` + `all_pairs`, lo = min(dense) − max(standard) and hi = max(dense) − min(standard), which is exactly the card's rule.

47	### metric_not_capturable: K3, K6, K7 (and K4's scope)
48	- **Why.** Per-pose DockQ must come from a pinned DockQ evaluator that alone has the native references (PC:23, 36). The draft has no such role:
49	  - adapters run only the arm's program and may not compute metrics;
50	  - `data.json` exposes every input to the arms;
51	  - `sealed_extraction` uses U54's kinds, which return one number per file (a JSON Pointer, or the *last* regex match, `s12/PROMPT.md:56`). So "best of 50" (a maximum) and "the pose ranked first" (the first match) cannot be extracted.
52	- **K4.** Its timing scope is the complete workflow, including DockQ (PC:68). Without an evaluator, A0's and A1's walls exclude DockQ, so K4 would be decided on a scope other than the sealed one.

If A1 fails on every replicate of an input, that input has zero pairs and is **supported**. Fix: an invocation with a nonzero `rc`, a timeout or no wrapper file makes its pair *missing*, and agreement with `n = 0` is void with reason `missing_values`.
61	- **(b) Nulls drop out of metric comparisons.**
62	  - K5: a timed-out or failed dense invocation becomes null and vanishes from `unpaired` differences. The remaining replicates can then give "supported", but the card records that run as unavailable at that tier (PC:29, 107) and the seed requires overruns to be preserved.
63	  - K6/K7: the same drop gives a gain or loss from the surviving replicates, while the card says "Missing/timeout arms mean unavailable comparison" (PC:29).

68	- **K1.** One output has one tolerance for every number in the file.

70	  - The 50 decoys are 50 files, but an output maps to one path.
71	  - Fix: an optional `select` per output, either a regex whose capture groups the *trusted comparator* keeps in order, or column indices. Also allow an output path to be an ordered list or a sorted glob of files, concatenated by the comparator. Adapters then never need to rewrite outputs.

83	  - `system.json` adds `ldd` of each executable and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,uuid`. At present only `box.type` implies the GPU model.

86	- **Why.** The harness agent still writes every adapter, and nothing checks that the arms share identical flags and differ only in the declared axis (PC:23, 40–48). Criteria are hidden by prompt wording only ("prompts name it and never `C/`"). Nothing states that agents cannot read `C/` or the design path.
87	- **Fix.**
88	  - Add an optional sealed `arms[].argv`, the exact published command line, passed as `CMP_ARGV`. The pipeline checks that the adapter executes it, for example by having the wrapper log the executed argv.
89	  - Require the design source and `C/` to lie outside every agent's readable roots.

92	- **Arms.** All three are published MEGADOCK binaries and flags, including A0's thread and affinity settings, so `arm_not_runnable` does not apply.
93	- **Order.** Each round contains every (arm, case) pair once, shuffled from `order_seed`; a round is the card's balanced block (PC:30, 106).
94	- **Sealing.** The comparison seal, the arms seal and the scorer's re-check are sound.
95	- **Reference.** Per-input values from a named previous run are sound for K5.
96	- **K5's split outcomes.** Mixed replicates come out `inconclusive` rather than `not_supported`. Only "supported" means "within tier", so the reading is unchanged.
97	
98	## For the owner
99	- This was the operator's single revision, and the verdict is still `partial`. The decision on the six fixes above is yours.
100	- The two largest are the trusted evaluator (K3, K4's scope, K6, K7) and the missing-value rule (K1–K3, K5–K7). Both are additions.

102	  - the source of the tolerances atol, rtol, eps_xyz and eps_eval;
103	  - approval of the main run above USD 20 (PC:75 projects USD 49.48).

| leaks `other` (sealed argv; `C/` unreadable) | **not met** | Arms are still chosen by agent-written adapters, and `C/` is hidden from prompts only |
| K1 shape (outputs, elementwise_abs, per_input_all, paired, all_pairs) | expressible, but see K1 | |
| K2 comparator `other` (symmetric base) | **not met** | `elementwise_abs_plus_rel` uses `abs(b)` |
| K3 shape | the comparator is expressible, but the values cannot be produced | |
| K4 shape (trusted_wall, pooled_mean, paired, bootstrap, ratio of means) | met as a statistic | See K4 for the timing scope |
| K5 shape (per_input_each, unpaired, all_pairs, previous-run reference) | expressible | Null handling and the timeout are wrong (see K5) |
| K6/K7 shape (sealed_extraction, per_input_each, unpaired, all_pairs, abs) | the statistic is expressible | The values cannot be produced (see K6/K7) |

Several s14 items can now be expressed **without a contract change**. A later design must use the following:
- **Gating of K4–K7 on K1–K3** (PC:65, 102). Write the agreement phase as its own design (K1–K3, A0 and A1, 1 replicate, matching "1 invocation per arm/case", PC:101). Launch the main design only if every agreement comparison is `supported`. The draft's split rule allows this.
- **Gain/loss sign for K6/K7** (PC:29). Write each as two one-sided superiority comparisons, `higher_better` (gain iff lo > m) and `lower_better` (loss iff hi < −m). With `unpaired` + `all_pairs`, lo = min(dense) − max(standard) and hi = max(dense) − min(standard), which is exactly the card's rule.
- **K5's three tiers.** Use three comparisons, each with a reference that maps the 4 cases to that tier's seconds. The main design then holds K4 + 3 + 4 = 8 comparisons, within the cap of 12.
- **K4's strict "> 1.05"** (PC:29). Set `threshold` to the next double above 1.05, so that `lo >= threshold` is equivalent to `lo > 1.05`.

## Missing items and problems, with the smallest fix for each

### metric_not_capturable: K3, K6, K7 (and K4's scope)
- **Why.** Per-pose DockQ must come from a pinned DockQ evaluator that alone has the native references (PC:23, 36). The draft has no such role:
  - adapters run only the arm's program and may not compute metrics;
  - `data.json` exposes every input to the arms;
  - `sealed_extraction` uses U54's kinds, which return one number per file (a JSON Pointer, or the *last* regex match, `s12/PROMPT.md:56`). So "best of 50" (a maximum) and "the pose ranked first" (the first match) cannot be extracted.
- **K4.** Its timing scope is the complete workflow, including DockQ (PC:68). Without an evaluator, A0's and A1's walls exclude DockQ, so K4 would be decided on a scope other than the sealed one.
- **Smallest fix.**
  1. Add an optional design field `evaluator: {what, references}`, with the references held in `C/` and in no view.
  2. Add a sealed adapter `harness/evaluate.sh` that runs the published, pinned evaluator. The trusted wrapper runs it after the arm's adapter in the same invocation, and only it receives `CMP_REFERENCE` and `CMP_EVAL_OUT`. Its wall time counts toward the arm's `wall_s` when a design flag `timing_includes_evaluator` is true.
  3. Allow `cmp_files` and `cmp_extract` to name evaluator files.
  4. Add a `reduce` field to extraction rules (`first`, `last`, `max`, `min`, applied to all regex matches or to a JSON array).

### statistic_unfit: K1, K2, K3, K5, K6, K7
- **(a) Vacuous agreement.** Agreement takes only replicates "where both arms ran with rc 0", and is supported "when every pair agrees and none is missing". If A1 fails on every replicate of an input, that input has zero pairs and is **supported**. Fix: an invocation with a nonzero `rc`, a timeout or no wrapper file makes its pair *missing*, and agreement with `n = 0` is void with reason `missing_values`.
- **(b) Nulls drop out of metric comparisons.**
  - K5: a timed-out or failed dense invocation becomes null and vanishes from `unpaired` differences. The remaining replicates can then give "supported", but the card records that run as unavailable at that tier (PC:29, 107) and the seed requires overruns to be preserved.
  - K6/K7: the same drop gives a gain or loss from the surviving replicates, while the card says "Missing/timeout arms mean unavailable comparison" (PC:29).
  - Fix: a per-comparison field `missing: "drop" | "void" | "fail"`. `fail` makes that unit `not_supported` (K5); `void` makes it void with reason `missing_values` (K6, K7, agreement). Record `n_missing` per row.

### margin_rule_unfit: K1, K2
- **K2.** The card seals |a − b| ≤ atol + rtol·max(|a|, |b|) (PC:58). The draft's base is `abs(b)` only, which is stricter and asymmetric, so a "not supported" can be wrong. Fix: add the comparator `"elementwise_abs_plus_rel_symmetric"` with base `max(abs(a), abs(b))`.
- **K1.** One output has one tolerance for every number in the file.
  - MEGADOCK's ranked output holds the rotation/translation entries and the scores on the same lines. Exact identity of the transforms (atol 0) cannot be checked without also requiring identical scores, and GPU scores are not reproducible (s13 §2: 39 distinct hashes over 40 files).
  - The 50 decoys are 50 files, but an output maps to one path.
  - Fix: an optional `select` per output, either a regex whose capture groups the *trusted comparator* keeps in order, or column indices. Also allow an output path to be an ordered list or a sorted glob of files, concatenated by the comparator. Adapters then never need to rewrite outputs.

### budget_unfit: K5
- **Why.** The only timeout is the time left in `budget_s`. The card's per-invocation cap at the largest frozen tier (PC:107) cannot be expressed, and one hung dense invocation consumes every later round.
- **Fix.** Add an optional design field `timeout_s` (one number, or a map per arm and input). The timeout becomes min(`timeout_s`, time left). A timeout is recorded as `"timeout"` and handled by the `missing` rule above.

### compute_unfit: compute_facts
- **(a) Billed allocation (s15 `other`).** FINAL.json's `usd` is the billed allocation, including setup, idle and failed work (PC:68, 111–112). The draft records only attribution (`wall_s × price`). `run_box_usd` (`SCHEMAS.md:337`) is a run-level number that treats an active box's end as the accounting time, and nothing marks it as an estimate. Fix:
  - add `allocation: {started_utc, ended_utc, hours, usd, final}` from `C/box.json`, refreshed at takeaways when the matching record has `ended_utc` (`SCHEMAS.md:332–333`); `final` is false otherwise;
  - rename the per-row and per-arm `usd` to `attributed_usd`.
- **(b) Versions and hardware identity.** The card pins executable hashes, linked FFTW/cuFFT/CUDA/OpenMP versions and GPU identity (PC:22). Fix:
  - the pipeline records the SHA-256 of each arm's executable, named in `versions.sh` output as `{arm: {version, executable}}`;
  - `system.json` adds `ldd` of each executable and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,uuid`. At present only `box.type` implies the GPU model.

### leaks_or_biases (s15 `other`, unchanged from s14 problem 9)
- **Why.** The harness agent still writes every adapter, and nothing checks that the arms share identical flags and differ only in the declared axis (PC:23, 40–48). Criteria are hidden by prompt wording only ("prompts name it and never `C/`"). Nothing states that agents cannot read `C/` or the design path.
- **Fix.**
  - Add an optional sealed `arms[].argv`, the exact published command line, passed as `CMP_ARGV`. The pipeline checks that the adapter executes it, for example by having the wrapper log the executed argv.
  - Require the design source and `C/` to lie outside every agent's readable roots.

## Not problems
- **Arms.** All three are published MEGADOCK binaries and flags, including A0's thread and affinity settings, so `arm_not_runnable` does not apply.
- **Order.** Each round contains every (arm, case) pair once, shuffled from `order_seed`; a round is the card's balanced block (PC:30, 106).
- **Sealing.** The comparison seal, the arms seal and the scorer's re-check are sound.
- **Reference.** Per-input values from a named previous run are sound for K5.
- **K5's split outcomes.** Mixed replicates come out `inconclusive` rather than `not_supported`. Only "supported" means "within tier", so the reading is unchanged.

## For the owner
- This was the operator's single revision, and the verdict is still `partial`. The decision on the six fixes above is yours.
- The two largest are the trusted evaluator (K3, K4's scope, K6, K7) and the missing-value rule (K1–K3, K5–K7). Both are additions.
- Still open from s13 §5, and not affected by this check:
  - the source of the tolerances atol, rtol, eps_xyz and eps_eval;
  - approval of the main run above USD 20 (PC:75 projects USD 49.48).
- s15 sealed no predictions, so `outcomes.json` is empty. This step runs no test.
- Next action: stop, `contract_gap`.

- **Gating.** K4 runs only after K1–K3 pass (PC:30, 65). The vocabulary has no field for gating, so it stays a required contract item from s14 problem 3 (`after: [K1, K2, K3]`, outcome `gated`).

### K5: A2 within per-case tier seconds (PC:97, 107)
**Shape:** `trusted_wall`, `per_input_each`, `unpaired`, `all_pairs`, margin `none`, `previous_run`.
- **Reference.** 4 cases × 3 tiers. They are frozen by the card's formula from walls measured in the calibration run (run 1), before run 2 (PC:96–97). So the origin is `previous_run`. The design must name that run and the formula, and seal the 12 values.
- **Decision unit.** Per case and per tier, reported, never averaged (PC:29, 111). A dense invocation that times out or fails is recorded as unavailable at that tier. It is never dropped and never counted as DockQ 0 (PC:29, 107). Nulls must therefore fail the tier rather than leave the pairing (s14 problem 2, `missing: "fail"`).
- **Interval.** `all_pairs` here means that every dense replicate finishes within the tier. The card does not state this rule word for word. It is the reading most consistent with PC:107 ("incomplete search unavailable at that tier") and the card's worst-case treatment elsewhere, and the sealed design must state it.

### K6 (rank-1 DockQ) and K7 (best-of-50 DockQ): A2 vs A1 (PC:29)
**Shape:** `sealed_extraction`, `per_input_each`, `unpaired`, `all_pairs`, `abs`, reference `none`.
- **Metric origin.** A rule fixed before the run reads the scalar from the trusted evaluator's per-pose DockQ for each arm's own output: rank 1 is the pose with the highest MEGADOCK score, and best-of-50 is the maximum over the 50 retained poses (PC:36). The two are separate extractions, and rank 1 is never inferred from best-of-50 (PC:29).
- **Pairing and interval.** The card's rule is gain iff min(dense) − max(standard) > margin + 2·eps_eval, and loss iff max(dense) − min(standard) < −(margin + 2·eps_eval). Taking every cross pair (i, j) of unpaired replicates and requiring all of them to clear the margin gives exactly min − max. That is `unpaired` + `all_pairs`. The paired-replicate form would be more liberal than the card (s14, K6/K7 row).
- **Margin.** abs, 0.01 + 2·eps_eval (PC:29).
- **Still outside the vocabulary.** The rule must report gain, loss or unresolved per case and per eligible tier, which is s14's `sign` field. Its eligibility depends on K5's per-tier outcome, and it is gated on K1–K3.

## 2. Fixes

**inputs: `one_input_per_invocation`.** The draft passes all inputs to one invocation (PROMPT.md:57, `CMP_INPUTS` = the view's inputs), so `process_wall` is shared by the 4 cases. K4 and K5 need per-case trusted walls, and the card runs "all 3 arms per case in randomized order" (PC:30). All arms take the same 4 pinned cases, so `inputs_differ_by_arm` does not apply. Run 1's synthetic fixtures feed the evaluator and tolerance analysis, not the arms.

**budget: `design_sets_budget`, `split_into_runs`.**
- The draft's only timeout is the time left in the shared evaluate budget (PROMPT.md:58). The card needs a per-invocation cap equal to the largest frozen tier (PC:107), and a phase timer checked against the 12 h ceiling before any box command.
- The card's phases need repair, then calibration (3 h, PC:85–86), then freeze, then agreement (2 h) and main (4 h) with a 2 h report reserve and a 12 h hard stop (PC:102, 107, 112). The tiers and tolerances must be frozen from run 1 before run 2 (PC:96), so K1–K7 cannot be decided in one run.
- Run 2 projects USD 49.48 (PC:75), above the USD 20 rule, so it needs owner approval (s13 §5).

**compute: `per_invocation_rows`, `exclude_overhead`, `software_versions`, `cpu_identity`, `other`.**
- `per_invocation_rows`: K4's bootstrap and K5's per-case tiers need each invocation's wall, not only the per-arm sums the draft writes (PROMPT.md:60).
- `exclude_overhead`: the arm's subprocess only, not link setup or fetches. The card reports cold setup and retrieval separately (PC:68).
- `software_versions`: CUDA, cuFFT, driver, FFTW and each binary's hash are pinned (PC:22). The draft's hardware record has the driver only.
- `cpu_identity`: A0 runs on the host CPU with 26 OpenMP threads and fixed affinity (PC:22, 24). The CPU wall is half of K4's ratio.
- **`other` (billed allocation).** FINAL.json's `usd` is the billed allocation: hours × price including setup, idle and failed work, with allocation start and end (PC:68, 111–112; s13 §3). The draft's per-arm `usd` is receipt wall × price (PROMPT.md:60), which is compute attribution. **What it needs** (s14 problem 8): an `allocation` record `{started_utc, ended_utc, hours, usd, final}` from `C/box.json`, refreshed when the allocation ends, with `final: false` marking an estimated bill; and per-arm `usd` renamed `attributed_usd`. No listed code describes the bill.

**leaks: `adapter_no_metrics`, `view_text_screened`, `other`.**
- `adapter_no_metrics`: in the draft, adapters report the metrics (PROMPT.md:59). With the shapes above, every number comes from the trusted comparator, the sealed extraction or the trusted wall. DockQ comes from the pinned evaluator, which alone has the natives (PC:23). An adapter therefore cannot shape a result.
- `view_text_screened`: the science step that writes the design's free text owns this check.
- **`other` (arms differ only in the declared axis, and criteria cannot be reached).** The card requires identical shared flags across arms (PC:23, 40–48). I did not choose `separate_adapter_authors`, because different authors still would not guarantee identical flags. **What it needs** (s14 problem 9):
  - a sealed `arms[].argv` per arm (the exact published command line), which the pipeline compares against the command each adapter executes;
  - the design source and `C/` outside every agent's readable roots, so margins and references cannot be reached by reading files, not only kept out of prompts.

## 3. Still open for the owner (unchanged from s13 §5)
These shapes do not depend on the choices below:
- The tolerance source for atol, rtol, eps_xyz and eps_eval (K1–K3, and the 2·eps_eval term in K6 and K7).
- Approval of run 2 above USD 20.

## 4. Counts and next action
- `other` appears 3 times in SHAPES.json: K2's comparator, compute and leaks.
- s14 sealed no predictions, so `outcomes.json` is empty.
- This step runs no test and makes no predictions.
- Next action: stop, `contract_gap`, for the operator's single revision of U57/U58.

51	- Purpose: a calibration run measures a tree card's load-bearing GUESS and PROXY inputs on the card's own protocol, and the measured values return to the card. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gap G2 of the blind-02 science route): the tree's calibration record names those inputs, but nothing passed the record to an m5 run or wrote a measurement back, so a run's result could not be read against the card's value. A measured input that does not hold refutes the card's value; that is a result and never fails a stage. Science checks s10 and s11 (2026-11-03) fixed the rest: no agent of the run sees the card's values, bands, gate thresholds, predictions or anchor value; how each input is read from the run's output is fixed before the workload runs and applied by the pipeline, not by a harness script; the card record is sealed before any box command; where the card sets a gate on an input, the gate decides it. Without `args.card`, every stage is unchanged.
52	- Optional `args.card` is an object with exactly the keys `result` and `key`, and optionally `bands`. `result` is a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a tree run's `result.json`; `key` is a non-empty string. The card's record is the entry of that file's `calibration` array whose `key` equals `key`. It must have `state` `"calibration_required"` and a non-empty `required` array whose items each have a unique string `id` matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$` and `basis` `"GUESS"` or `"PROXY"`. `bands`, when present, maps some of those ids to `{"abs": x}` with `x` a finite number above 0: absolute bands fixed before the run by whoever launches it, for inputs a multiplicative band cannot judge. An invalid `args.card`, a missing or unreadable file, invalid JSON, no matching record, any other state, an invalid `required` or `bands`, or `args.card` together with `args.units_check` or `args.units_probe` fails intake with `error_class: parse` before any agent call.
53	- Optional `args.pipeline_commit` is a string naming the commit of the pipeline copy the run executes; `launch.js` writes it into every m5 `args.json` (the short commit it already records in RUN.md, or null when unknown). It changes no behaviour.
54	- Before the intake agent call and any box command, the pipeline writes, atomically and in this order: `C/card.json`, exactly `{source, source_sha256, record, bands}` (`source` the absolute path of `result`, `source_sha256` the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of its exact bytes, `record` the matching record unchanged, `bands` the launch bands or `{}`); `C/card_seal.json`, exactly `{card_sha256, sealed_utc}` (the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of `C/card.json` and a UTC ISO time); and `A/card_inputs.json`, exactly `{inputs, anchor}`. `inputs` has one entry per `required` item in order, each exactly `{id, name, unit, measured_by, phase}`, with `phase` the item's `phase.what` or null and `name`/`unit` null when absent. `anchor` is `{"what": <the record anchor's what>}` when the record's anchor has a finite numeric `published_value`, otherwise null. `A/card_inputs.json` holds no value, basis, band, gate, cost line, budget, prediction or published value. Every later read of the card uses `C/card.json`, never `result`.
55	- Agents see only `A/card_inputs.json`. Card-mode prompts name it and never name `C/` or `result`; the existing rule that agents never read `control/` stands. Intake prompt, card mode only: this run calibrates the listed inputs, and EXECUTION.json's representative workload is the protocol of the phases they name (their `measured_by` and `phase`), not another workload. Harness prompt, card mode only: the representative run must write outputs from which each listed input, and the anchor quantity when `anchor` is non-null, can be read, and the harness agent declares in `harness/card_extract.json` how each one is read; no harness script computes, writes or asserts a card value.
56	- `A/harness/card_extract.json` is exactly `{"rules": [...]}`: one rule per `inputs` entry in order, then one rule with id `"anchor"` when `anchor` is non-null. Each rule is exactly `{id, file, kind, expr}`. `file` is a relative path under the run's `out/`, one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none `.` or `..`. `kind` `"json"`: `expr` is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into that file, and the value there must be a finite JSON number (never a boolean). `kind` `"regex"`: `expr` is a Python `re` pattern with exactly one capturing group; the file is read as UTF-8 with replacement, the last match's group is parsed with `float()` and must be finite. With `args.harness_from`, the source harness directory must also hold `card_extract.json`, copied like the other scripts. The pipeline validates the file after harness generation or copy and before the harness upload; a missing or invalid file fails reproduce with `error_class: parse` before the upload. It then writes `C/card_extract_seal.json`, exactly `{extract_sha256, sealed_utc}`. No repair changes `card_extract.json`.
57	- Scoring: after `run_anchors.sh` exits 0 and its output gate passes, before anchor scoring and whatever the anchors score, the pipeline runs `python3 -I m5/score_card.py <C dir> <A/harness/card_extract.json> <A/results/reproduce/out dir> --run <run tag> --commit <pipeline_commit, or - when null>`. The script first checks the SHA-256 of `C/card.json` against `C/card_seal.json` and that of `card_extract.json` against `C/card_extract_seal.json`; then applies each rule to the fetched outputs (a missing or unreadable file, no match, or a value that is not a finite number gives null); then writes `C/card_scored.json` atomically, exactly `{key, run, pipeline_commit, box_type, box_started_utc, card_sha256, extract_sha256, predictions, anchor, rows, inputs_total, measured_total, holds_total, refuted_total}`. `box_type` and `box_started_utc` come from `C/box.json` (`type`, `started_utc`), null when unavailable; `pipeline_commit` is null for `-`; `predictions` is the record's `predictions` unchanged (null when absent).
58	  - `anchor` is null when `A/card_inputs.json` has no anchor; otherwise exactly `{published_value, tolerance, measured_value, difference, passed}`: `published_value` and `tolerance` copy the record anchor's; `difference` is measured minus published, null when unmeasured; `passed` is `abs(difference) <= t` for a finite nonnegative numeric tolerance `t` or `{"abs": t}`, `abs(difference) <= t * abs(published_value)` for `{"rel": t}`, and null for any other tolerance or when unmeasured. The anchor never decides an input.
59	  - `rows` follows `required` order, one row per item, each exactly `{id, name, unit, basis, value, band_source, band_lo, band_hi, measured_value, verdict, gate_passed, decided_by, decision, rule}`. `name` and `unit` copy the item's (null when absent); `basis` and `value` copy the item's; `rule` is the item's extraction rule without its `id`.
60	  - Band: a launch band (`bands[id]`) or else the item's own `band` when it is `{"abs": x}` gives `band_source` `"launch"` or `"card"` and `[value - x, value + x]` when `value` is a finite number. 61	  - `verdict` is `"not_measured"` when `measured_value` is null; otherwise `"no_band"` when the band is null; otherwise `"within_band"` when `band_lo <= measured_value <= band_hi`, `"below_band"` below it and `"above_band"` above it.
62	  - `gate_passed` is null unless the item's `phase.gate` is an object whose `on` equals the item's `id`, whose `op` is `">="` or `"<="` and whose `value` is a finite number, and `measured_value` is a number; then it is the boolean `measured_value <op> gate.value`.
63	  - `decided_by` is `"gate"` when `gate_passed` is a boolean, otherwise `"band"` when `verdict` is `within_band`, `below_band` or `above_band`, otherwise null. `decision` is `"holds"` or `"refuted"` by the gate (`gate_passed` true or false) when it decides, otherwise by the band (`within_band` holds; `below_band` and `above_band` refute); `"not_measured"` when unmeasured; `"undecidable"` when measured with neither a gate nor a band.
64	  - `inputs_total` counts rows, `measured_total` rows with a number, `holds_total` and `refuted_total` the rows with those decisions.
65	  - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails reproduce with `error_class: parse`.
66	- Card rows never change reproduce's status, gate or `run_valid`: they are measured and reported, as references are.
67	- Reproduce facts add optional `card_inputs`, `card_measured`, `card_holds` and `card_refuted`, the four totals as nonnegative integers. All four are null outside card mode, on SKIPPED/stub records, and whenever `C/card_scored.json` was not written; records without them stay valid.
