69	## Card write-back and re-judging (U56)
70	- Purpose: return a calibration's measurements to the card as MEASURED plan numbers, with the run's identity, and re-judge the card's plan and cost with them (science check s11, 2026-11-03). The card's state comes from every run that measured it, not the latest. Re-judging uses the tree's own deterministic cost evaluation and plan gate; no model is called and no model judge is re-run.
71	- `node m5/card_resolve.js <result.json> <run root> [<run root> ...] --out <file>` reads each run root's `control/card.json`, `control/card_seal.json` and `control/card_scored.json`, and writes `<file>` atomically, never over one of its inputs, as exactly `{source, source_sha256, calibration}`. `source` is the absolute path of `result.json` and `source_sha256` the SHA-256 of its bytes; `result.json` itself is never modified. A run whose `card.json` SHA-256 differs from its seal, whose `source_sha256` differs from the result's, a missing or invalid file, or a key with no record exits 1 and writes nothing.
72	- `calibration` is the result's `calibration` array; records no run names are unchanged. A named record (same `key`) gets `resolved`: its existing entries, then one entry per scored row, runs in argument order, each exactly `{run, pipeline_commit, box_type, box_started_utc, id, measured_value, verdict, decided_by, decision, number}`. `number` is null when `measured_value` is null; otherwise the MEASURED plan number `{id, name, unit, basis: "MEASURED", value, differs_in: [], command, output, output_line, machine}` with `value` the measured value, `command` `"bash harness/run_command.sh"`, `output` the rule's `file` prefixed by `<run root basename>/agent/results/reproduce/out/`, `output_line` the rule's `kind` and `expr` joined by `": "`, and `machine` the `box_type`.
73	- State, from all entries of all runs: `"refuted"` when any entry for a `required` id has decision `refuted`; otherwise `"calibrated"` when every `required` id has at least one `holds` entry; otherwise unchanged.
74	- Re-judging: a named record that has `judged` (see CONTRACT.md, U55) also gets `rejudged`, exactly `{measured_ids, plan_usd_before, plan_usd_after, gate_action, gate_reasons, uncertain_after}`. The tool copies `judged.plan`, replaces each `numbers` entry whose id has at least one measured entry by that entry's fields without `rests_on`, `source_id`, `quote` and `page_setting`, merged with the MEASURED number above whose `value` is the median of all measured values for that id (the mean of the middle two for an even count) and whose provenance fields come from the latest such entry, then runs the tree's `cost_eval_plan(plan, judged.given)` and `gate_plan(plan, ev, judged.pick, judged.gate_args)` from `src/` (loaded in the build order, as `build.js` concatenates them). `measured_ids` lists the replaced ids in `required` order; `plan_usd_before` is the record's `plan_usd`; `plan_usd_after` is the new evaluation's `planned`; `gate_action` and `gate_reasons` are `gate_plan`'s `action` and `reasons`; `uncertain_after` lists the ids of the new evaluation's `uncertain`. A record without `judged` gets `rejudged: null`.

The card's state comes from every run that measured it, not the latest. Re-judging uses the tree's own deterministic cost evaluation and plan gate; no model is called and no model judge is re-run.
- `node m5/card_resolve.js <result.json> <run root> [<run root> ...] --out <file>` reads each run root's `control/card.json`, `control/card_seal.json` and `control/card_scored.json`, and writes `<file>` atomically, never over one of its inputs, as exactly `{source, source_sha256, calibration}`. `source` is the absolute path of `result.json` and `source_sha256` the SHA-256 of its bytes; `result.json` itself is never modified. A run whose `card.json` SHA-256 differs from its seal, whose `source_sha256` differs from the result's, a missing or invalid file, or a key with no record exits 1 and writes nothing.
- `calibration` is the result's `calibration` array; records no run names are unchanged. A named record (same `key`) gets `resolved`: its existing entries, then one entry per scored row, runs in argument order, each exactly `{run, pipeline_commit, box_type, box_started_utc, id, measured_value, verdict, decided_by, decision, number}`. `number` is null when `measured_value` is null; otherwise the MEASURED plan number `{id, name, unit, basis: "MEASURED", value, differs_in: [], command, output, output_line, machine}` with `value` the measured value, `command` `"bash harness/run_command.sh"`, `output` the rule's `file` prefixed by `<run root basename>/agent/results/reproduce/out/`, `output_line` the rule's `kind` and `expr` joined by `": "`, and `machine` the `box_type`.
- State, from all entries of all runs: `"refuted"` when any entry for a `required` id has decision `refuted`; otherwise `"calibrated"` when every `required` id has at least one `holds` entry; otherwise unchanged.
- Re-judging: a named record that has `judged` (see CONTRACT.md, U55) also gets `rejudged`, exactly `{measured_ids, plan_usd_before, plan_usd_after, gate_action, gate_reasons, uncertain_after}`. The tool copies `judged.plan`, replaces each `numbers` entry whose id has at least one measured entry by that entry's fields without `rests_on`, `source_id`, `quote` and `page_setting`, merged with the MEASURED number above whose `value` is the median of all measured values for that id (the mean of the middle two for an even count) and whose provenance fields come from the latest such entry, then runs the tree's `cost_eval_plan(plan, judged.given)` and `gate_plan(plan, ev, judged.pick, judged.gate_args)` from `src/` (loaded in the build order, as `build.js` concatenates them). `measured_ids` lists the replaced ids in `required` order; `plan_usd_before` is the record's `plan_usd`; `plan_usd_after` is the new evaluation's `planned`; `gate_action` and `gate_reasons` are `gate_plan`'s `action` and `reasons`; `uncertain_after` lists the ids of the new evaluation's `uncertain`. A record without `judged` gets `rejudged: null`.

content.content:
- Optional `uncertainty` is null or exactly `{kind, value}`, where `kind` is `"standard_error"`, `"standard_deviation"` or `"interval_halfwidth"` and `value` is finite and nonnegative. It records published uncertainty where available and never affects scoring.
  - Optional `comparison` is one of `"=="` (the default), `">"`, `">="`, `"<"`, or `"<="`. For `"=="`, an anchor passes when `abs(measured_value - published_value) <= resolved_absolute_tolerance`. For inequalities, it passes when `measured_value <comparison> published_value`; tolerance is ignored and may be 0 or null. Intake should specify `comparison` when the published criterion is a threshold.
  - `tolerance` is a finite nonnegative number (absolute tolerance), or an object with exactly one key: `{"abs": x}` or `{"rel": x}`, where `x` is finite and nonnegative. For `"=="`, relative tolerance resolves to `x * abs(published_value)`; a zero reference therefore requires exact agreement.
- baseline.json: non-empty repo, build_commands, run_commands and published_configuration, plus commit or pin. `build_commands` lists every command that builds or installs the baseline, including package-manager installs of released binaries, and is never empty. The intake prompt states both. The intake prompt names every key the completeness check reads exactly as the check reads it, as a JSON key: in baseline.json `repo`, `build_commands`, `run_commands`, `published_configuration`, and `commit` or `pin` (`pin` is any non-empty immutable identifier, such as a release, tag or content hash, when no commit exists); in EXECUTION.json `representative_scale`, `inputs`, `outputs` and `timing_scope`. It states that the check reads only these key names, so an equivalent value under another key does not count. The completeness check itself is unchanged.
- EXECUTION.json: non-empty representative_scale, inputs, outputs and timing_scope. Optional `stage_budgets_s` supplies positive integer seconds in [1, 999999999], with keys `setup`, `anchors`, `profile`, `method_setup`, `method_run`, `tests`, `evaluate`. Keys `method_setup`, `method_run`, `tests` and `evaluate` each resolve independently from `EXECUTION.json.stage_budgets_s`, then `args.stage_budgets_s`, then defaults: method_setup=1200, method_run=1200, tests=900, evaluate=2400. Keys `setup`, `anchors` and `profile` resolve as the next bullet states (U47). Legacy `timeout_s` and `timeouts` no longer set pipeline box budgets. Every box command passes its resolved budget as `boxrun --timeout`. Harness uploads/probes use setup; implementation uploads, baseline snapshots, patch application and integrity checks use method_setup; evaluation uploads/integrity checks use method_setup. Script retries under the other keys retain the original budget.
- Finish-first timing for the baseline workload (U47; owner direction 2026-10-30: intake's budgets are recorded estimates, not timeouts; a run is limited by a 12 h hard ceiling; a reproduction-only result counts). Keys `setup`, `anchors` and `profile` resolve from `args.stage_budgets_s` when the key is present there. Otherwise the budget is the time left before the run ceiling when that box command starts: `run_ceiling_s` minus the whole seconds elapsed since the pipeline script started, rounded down. `run_ceiling_s` is the optional `args.run_ceiling_s`, an integer in [1, 999999999], default 43200 (12 h); any other value is an invalid budget and is handled as an invalid stage budget is. Every box command under these keys resolves its budget when it starts: each setup and anchors attempt, each rerun after a repair, each identical retry, every harness upload, the box probe and its upload, the fixed profiler and the concurrency probe. When the time left is below 1 s, the command does not run and its step fails as a timeout does (`error_class: timeout`, exit 3). `EXECUTION.json.stage_budgets_s` values for these three keys stay in EXECUTION.json unchanged and never set a timeout. Prompts that state setup, anchors or profile budgets give the seconds resolved when the prompt is built and say the figure is the time left before the run ceiling, not a target; one fixed scale and no scale search still apply. The other keys are unchanged. Run evidence (blind-01 run8, 2026-10-31): intake set a 1,200 s anchors budget; in two of three anchors attempts the representative-scale workload was still running at the budget, it completed only partly and wrote no measurements, and an authorized reader judged an anchors budget from a measured or published runtime the smallest fix; the materials were not implicated. The profile stage runs the same `run_command.sh`.
- Every harness, test-author, method-author and repair prompt states the budget for each script it writes. All require one fixed scale from EXECUTION.json, no scale search or doubling loops, and completion well within the budget. Baseline run_evaluation.sh and method run_anchors.sh use method_run per invocation; evaluate bounds each complete scorer, including all repetitions and curves.
- The intake passes only when the files are complete and found is true, data is "available", licence is not "restricted", and stock_environment is not false. Missing executable inputs and an explicit licence restriction block; missing published tolerances do not. A `licence` of "unknown" does not block: local experiments proceed under the owner's standing authorization (2026-10-30), which is recorded separately from licence evidence and never changes it. Intake records `licence` and `licence_basis` as the evidence shows and never relabels ambiguous coverage as permission. The intake prompt states that "unknown" stays "unknown" when permission is not established, that it does not stop the run, and that "restricted" does. `found` means a public benchmark with executable published code, command and inputs; a benchmark without published tolerances qualifies, with its published values recorded as references. The intake prompt states this.
- Intake facts add optional `anchored` (boolean): true exactly when anchors.json holds at least one anchor. Every executed intake stage emits it once anchors.json validates; it is null when anchors.json is missing or invalid and on SKIPPED/stub records. `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` shows it among the intake gate flags. A run whose intake has `anchored=false` is unanchored: its claims concern the workload as published and run, not agreement with published values.
- An intake FAIL signature names the failed gate conditions in v1 `blockers`, from the existing blocker vocabulary and in this fixed order: `licence` when the `licence` fact is "restricted", `data_unavailable` when the `data` fact is "partial", "unavailable" or "unknown", and `env_irreproducible` when the `stock_environment` fact is false. Each condition is read from the facts the record carries, whatever else failed (missing reply, incomplete or invalid files, or `found` false); a null or absent fact adds no blocker. When no condition applies, and for every PASS, SKIPPED and stub intake, `blockers` stays `["none"]`. Intake `exit_code`, `exit_kind` and `error_class` are unchanged. `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` lists these blockers in its Blockers section as for any stage.
- Intake facts add optional `licence_basis`, the basis of the licence judgement for the least-covered item among the benchmark code and its required inputs. It is the first of these values that applies to any item, in this fixed order: `"unreachable"` (the licence evidence for the item could not be fetched), `"none"` (no licence, terms of use or owner statement found for the item), `"owner"` (the item's only basis is a permission stated by the run's owner in the brief), `"distribution"` (the item's only basis is a licence of the repository, package or archive that distributes it, and that licence does not state that it covers the item), `"explicit"` (a licence or terms of use states that it covers the item, by name, by path, or as the whole repository, package or archive). The intake prompt defines these values and asks for the fact; a value outside the list makes the reply invalid, as for any other fact. It is null when the reply omits it, and on SKIPPED and stub records. It never changes the gate, the `licence` fact, `blockers` or any other fact. Signatures carry it as an enum fact, and `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` shows it among the intake gate flags.
- Full JSON content is included in the harness prompt and every setup and anchor repair prompt. Agents must use discovered paths and versions and never hard-code a toolkit path absent from the probe. Select a CUDA toolkit root discovered in `probe.json` with both `include/cuda_runtime.h` and `lib64/libcudart.so`, checking both with `ls` on the box from the scripts. Pass it explicitly via `CUDAToolkit_ROOT` or `-DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=<root>/bin/nvcc`, and prepend `<root>/bin` to `PATH`. Never rely on `/usr/bin/nvcc` when a complete toolkit root exists. A tool or system library the published baseline needs but the stock image lacks may be installed with `sudo apt-get install -y` from any source the probe reports in `apt_enabled_sources` (after `sudo apt-get update`), once `apt-cache policy <package>` shows an install candidate. Never add repositories, keys or source lines, and never enable a commented or disabled source. Setup prints each package it installs and its installed version (`dpkg-query -W <package>`). Otherwise only cmake may fall back to pip. If neither route applies, scripts must fail with a clear message. The harness prompt and every setup and anchors repair prompt state this rule. Run evidence (blind-01 run6, 2026-10-31): setup failed three times on a missing runtime library packaged in the Ubuntu archive (universe); the rule then allowed apt only from the CUDA/NVIDIA lines in `apt_sources`, so neither repair could install it.

## A/harness/ (written by the harness agent or copied from a previous run)
- Optional `args.harness_from` is a non-empty directory path to a previous run's `A/harness/`, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory. After a successful fresh box probe, the pipeline copies the exact bytes of `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` into the current `A/harness/` and skips the initial harness agent call. If present, `run_evaluation.sh` is copied too. Missing or unreadable required scripts, or an invalid argument, fail reproduce with `error_class: parse`; there is no fallback harness generation. Without this argument, harness generation is unchanged.
- Reuse writes script-owned `C/harness_source.json` as `{source, files}`. `source` is the absolute source harness directory; `files` maps each copied filename to `{sha256, modified}`. `sha256` is the lowercase 64-digit SHA-256 of the exact original copied bytes and remains unchanged after repair. `modified` starts false and becomes true after an accepted repair of that script, before its upload/rerun, even if that rerun fails. Reuse permits the same bounded setup and anchor repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors) as generated harnesses; every repair receives the fresh probe. Reuse adds no stage facts and does not reuse probe results, measurements, or stock verification.
- `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh`, `run_command.sh` are bash scripts. The pipeline invokes them as `bash harness/<name>` from one fresh `/tmp/m5-<uuid>` directory on the already-running operator-managed box. They share that directory across reproduce and profile. No dev lifecycle commands are issued. `BOX` and `FETCH` are inherited unchanged by `boxrun.sh`, including injected executables.
- wf exposes `agent.journal`, the absolute journal path. Cached journal events now include `model`, preserved from the successful result in the resume source. Cached answers retain model provenance but incur no new token usage. Failed attempts and unused shadow answers do not replace the answering family.
- New `C/stages/<stage>.json` receipts contain `{stage, status, wall_s, gpu_s, usd, model_family, notes}`, plus any stage-provided v1 overrides and measured token counts. Stage/status/model families use their existing enums. `notes` is an array with either no entries or the single fixed code `multiple_model_families`; no model text, prompts, filenames, or scientific facts are copied into it. These receipts are separate from `C/receipts/` box command receipts.
- Both serve and dev `lambda_serve.sh up` write `$HOME/.cache/metis-serve/box.json` atomically alongside `state.json`. Its keys are `{type, region, price_usd_h, started_utc}`: Lambda instance-type and region identifiers, a numeric hourly USD price, and a UTC ISO timestamp. Repeated state saves preserve the allocation's start. Confirmed `down` retains `box.json` and adds `ended_utc` (UTC ISO timestamp) and `hours` (nonnegative elapsed allocation hours, including startup and termination polling). State archival behavior is unchanged. The next `up` replaces this record for the new allocation.
- At the start of reproduce, the pipeline copies the current shared `box.json` to `C/box.json`, replacing any stale run copy. Missing box metadata leaves pricing unavailable and stage USD at zero. At takeaways, a matching allocation record can refresh the copy with its confirmed end; a different allocation never replaces the snapshot. If reproduce was skipped, takeaways snapshots the current allocation to account for any run overlap.
- Box receipts add numeric nonnegative `gpu_busy_s` and boolean `gpu_busy_known`. The detached remote script writes `<receipt-id>.gpu` beside its log, sampling `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits` immediately and every 2 seconds until the command exits or times out. Each finite utilization sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100 * 2` seconds; samples from every GPU are summed. Missing/invalid samples contribute nothing. No valid samples means `gpu_busy_s=0`, `gpu_busy_known=false`. Telemetry collection failure does not change command/fetch success. Sampling survives loss of the local polling process; the remote runner stops sampling before publishing its exit marker.
- Stage v1 `gpu_s` sums its box receipts' `gpu_busy_s`, including failed commands and retries. For stages with box receipts, `facts.gpu_busy_known` is true only when every receipt has valid busy telemetry; partial telemetry contributes its measured values while the flag stays false. Harness profile timing remains separate evidence and never substitutes for receipt GPU accounting. This supersedes the earlier statement that reproduce/profile always leave this flag false.
- Stage v1 `usd` is `sum(its box receipts' wall_s) / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h`, including uploads, probes, failed commands, polling/fetch time, and retries. Stage `wall_s` remains elapsed stage time and includes agent calls. No allocation or model-call envelopes are added.
- Takeaways facts optionally add `run_box_usd`, a finite nonnegative number or null; old v2 records without this key remain valid. The pipeline writes null for a SKIPPED takeaways stage; otherwise it writes the whole run's box charge here: the intersection of `[run start, takeaways accounting time]` with `[box.started_utc, box.ended_utc]`, multiplied by hourly price. An active box uses accounting time as its end. When timestamps or price are unavailable, it falls back to summed stage USD. This is a run summary, not extra stage spend; takeaways v1 `usd` retains only its own command attribution.
- `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` now has a Compute section: one row per stage with existing gate columns plus `wall_s`, `gpu_s`, `usd`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `model_family`; a box table; and run totals. The optional Python API is now `takeaway(records, raid=None, box=None)`. The CLI reads only validated signatures and sibling `C/box.json`; it does not read agent content. Run USD uses `facts.run_box_usd` when present, avoiding double-counting stage attribution; other totals preserve the existing launch/model-call preference and stage fallback.
- Operator box output whitelists only `type` and `price_usd_h`. Price must be a finite nonnegative JSON number (never a boolean); unavailable price renders `null`. Type is a fixed enum: `gpu_1x_a10`, `gpu_1x_a100`, `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4`, `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4_80gb`, `gpu_8x_a100`, `gpu_8x_a100_80gb_sxm4`, `gpu_1x_h100_pcie`, `gpu_1x_h100_sxm5`, `gpu_8x_h100_sxm5`, `gpu_1x_gh200`, `gpu_1x_h200`, `gpu_8x_h200_sxm5`, `gpu_1x_b200`, `gpu_8x_b200`, or `unknown`. Unknown types render `unknown`; region, timestamps, and all other box fields never enter operator output.

Every executed intake stage emits it once anchors.json validates; it is null when anchors.json is missing or invalid and on SKIPPED/stub records. `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` shows it among the intake gate flags. A run whose intake has `anchored=false` is unanchored: its claims concern the workload as published and run, not agreement with published values.
- An intake FAIL signature names the failed gate conditions in v1 `blockers`, from the existing blocker vocabulary and in this fixed order: `licence` when the `licence` fact is "restricted", `data_unavailable` when the `data` fact is "partial", "unavailable" or "unknown", and `env_irreproducible` when the `stock_environment` fact is false. Each condition is read from the facts the record carries, whatever else failed (missing reply, incomplete or invalid files, or `found` false); a null or absent fact adds no blocker. When no condition applies, and for every PASS, SKIPPED and stub intake, `blockers` stays `["none"]`. Intake `exit_code`, `exit_kind` and `error_class` are unchanged. `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` lists these blockers in its Blockers section as for any stage.
- Intake facts add optional `licence_basis`, the basis of the licence judgement for the least-covered item among the benchmark code and its required inputs. It is the first of these values that applies to any item, in this fixed order: `"unreachable"` (the licence evidence for the item could not be fetched), `"none"` (no licence, terms of use or owner statement found for the item), `"owner"` (the item's only basis is a permission stated by the run's owner in the brief), `"distribution"` (the item's only basis is a licence of the repository, package or archive that distributes it, and that licence does not state that it covers the item), `"explicit"` (a licence or terms of use states that it covers the item, by name, by path, or as the whole repository, package or archive). The intake prompt defines these values and asks for the fact; a value outside the list makes the reply invalid, as for any other fact. It is null when the reply omits it, and on SKIPPED and stub records. It never changes the gate, the `licence` fact, `blockers` or any other fact. Signatures carry it as an enum fact, and `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` shows it among the intake gate flags.
- Full JSON content is included in the harness prompt and every setup and anchor repair prompt. Agents must use discovered paths and versions and never hard-code a toolkit path absent from the probe. Select a CUDA toolkit root discovered in `probe.json` with both `include/cuda_runtime.h` and `lib64/libcudart.so`, checking both with `ls` on the box from the scripts. Pass it explicitly via `CUDAToolkit_ROOT` or `-DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=<root>/bin/nvcc`, and prepend `<root>/bin` to `PATH`. Never rely on `/usr/bin/nvcc` when a complete toolkit root exists. A tool or system library the published baseline needs but the stock image lacks may be installed with `sudo apt-get install -y` from any source the probe reports in `apt_enabled_sources` (after `sudo apt-get update`), once `apt-cache policy <package>` shows an install candidate. Never add repositories, keys or source lines, and never enable a commented or disabled source. Setup prints each package it installs and its installed version (`dpkg-query -W <package>`). Otherwise only cmake may fall back to pip. If neither route applies, scripts must fail with a clear message. The harness prompt and every setup and anchors repair prompt state this rule. Run evidence (blind-01 run6, 2026-10-31): setup failed three times on a missing runtime library packaged in the Ubuntu archive (universe); the rule then allowed apt only from the CUDA/NVIDIA lines in `apt_sources`, so neither repair could install it.

## A/harness/ (written by the harness agent or copied from a previous run)
- Optional `args.harness_from` is a non-empty directory path to a previous run's `A/harness/`, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory. After a successful fresh box probe, the pipeline copies the exact bytes of `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` into the current `A/harness/` and skips the initial harness agent call. If present, `run_evaluation.sh` is copied too. Missing or unreadable required scripts, or an invalid argument, fail reproduce with `error_class: parse`; there is no fallback harness generation. Without this argument, harness generation is unchanged.
- Reuse writes script-owned `C/harness_source.json` as `{source, files}`. `source` is the absolute source harness directory; `files` maps each copied filename to `{sha256, modified}`. `sha256` is the lowercase 64-digit SHA-256 of the exact original copied bytes and remains unchanged after repair. `modified` starts false and becomes true after an accepted repair of that script, before its upload/rerun, even if that rerun fails. Reuse permits the same bounded setup and anchor repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors) as generated harnesses; every repair receives the fresh probe. Reuse adds no stage facts and does not reuse probe results, measurements, or stock verification.
- `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh`, `run_command.sh` are bash scripts. The pipeline invokes them as `bash harness/<name>` from one fresh `/tmp/m5-<uuid>` directory on the already-running operator-managed box. They share that directory across reproduce and profile. No dev lifecycle commands are issued. `BOX` and `FETCH` are inherited unchanged by `boxrun.sh`, including injected executables.
- wf exposes `agent.journal`, the absolute journal path. Cached journal events now include `model`, preserved from the successful result in the resume source. Cached answers retain model provenance but incur no new token usage. Failed attempts and unused shadow answers do not replace the answering family.
- New `C/stages/<stage>.json` receipts contain `{stage, status, wall_s, gpu_s, usd, model_family, notes}`, plus any stage-provided v1 overrides and measured token counts. Stage/status/model families use their existing enums. `notes` is an array with either no entries or the single fixed code `multiple_model_families`; no model text, prompts, filenames, or scientific facts are copied into it. These receipts are separate from `C/receipts/` box command receipts.
- Both serve and dev `lambda_serve.sh up` write `$HOME/.cache/metis-serve/box.json` atomically alongside `state.json`. Its keys are `{type, region, price_usd_h, started_utc}`: Lambda instance-type and region identifiers, a numeric hourly USD price, and a UTC ISO timestamp. Repeated state saves preserve the allocation's start. Confirmed `down` retains `box.json` and adds `ended_utc` (UTC ISO timestamp) and `hours` (nonnegative elapsed allocation hours, including startup and termination polling). State archival behavior is unchanged. The next `up` replaces this record for the new allocation.
- At the start of reproduce, the pipeline copies the current shared `box.json` to `C/box.json`, replacing any stale run copy. Missing box metadata leaves pricing unavailable and stage USD at zero. At takeaways, a matching allocation record can refresh the copy with its confirmed end; a different allocation never replaces the snapshot. If reproduce was skipped, takeaways snapshots the current allocation to account for any run overlap.
- Box receipts add numeric nonnegative `gpu_busy_s` and boolean `gpu_busy_known`. The detached remote script writes `<receipt-id>.gpu` beside its log, sampling `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits` immediately and every 2 seconds until the command exits or times out. Each finite utilization sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100 * 2` seconds; samples from every GPU are summed. Missing/invalid samples contribute nothing. No valid samples means `gpu_busy_s=0`, `gpu_busy_known=false`. Telemetry collection failure does not change command/fetch success. Sampling survives loss of the local polling process; the remote runner stops sampling before publishing its exit marker.
- Stage v1 `gpu_s` sums its box receipts' `gpu_busy_s`, including failed commands and retries. For stages with box receipts, `facts.gpu_busy_known` is true only when every receipt has valid busy telemetry; partial telemetry contributes its measured values while the flag stays false. Harness profile timing remains separate evidence and never substitutes for receipt GPU accounting. This supersedes the earlier statement that reproduce/profile always leave this flag false.
- Stage v1 `usd` is `sum(its box receipts' wall_s) / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h`, including uploads, probes, failed commands, polling/fetch time, and retries. Stage `wall_s` remains elapsed stage time and includes agent calls. No allocation or model-call envelopes are added.
- Takeaways facts optionally add `run_box_usd`, a finite nonnegative number or null; old v2 records without this key remain valid. The pipeline writes null for a SKIPPED takeaways stage; otherwise it writes the whole run's box charge here: the intersection of `[run start, takeaways accounting time]` with `[box.started_utc, box.ended_utc]`, multiplied by hourly price. An active box uses accounting time as its end. When timestamps or price are unavailable, it falls back to summed stage USD. This is a run summary, not extra stage spend; takeaways v1 `usd` retains only its own command attribution.
- `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` now has a Compute section: one row per stage with existing gate columns plus `wall_s`, `gpu_s`, `usd`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `model_family`; a box table; and run totals. The optional Python API is now `takeaway(records, raid=None, box=None)`. The CLI reads only validated signatures and sibling `C/box.json`; it does not read agent content. Run USD uses `facts.run_box_usd` when present, avoiding double-counting stage attribution; other totals preserve the existing launch/model-call preference and stage fallback.
- Operator box output whitelists only `type` and `price_usd_h`. Price must be a finite nonnegative JSON number (never a boolean); unavailable price renders `null`. Type is a fixed enum: `gpu_1x_a10`, `gpu_1x_a100`, `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4`, `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4_80gb`, `gpu_8x_a100`, `gpu_8x_a100_80gb_sxm4`, `gpu_1x_h100_pcie`, `gpu_1x_h100_sxm5`, `gpu_8x_h100_sxm5`, `gpu_1x_gh200`, `gpu_1x_h200`, `gpu_8x_h200_sxm5`, `gpu_1x_b200`, `gpu_8x_b200`, or `unknown`. Unknown types render `unknown`; region, timestamps, and all other box fields never enter operator output.

## Run identity and agent chat names
- `args.blind` is a boolean, default false. `args.raid`, when supplied, is a non-empty single-line string and takes precedence over automatic selection. `launch.js stage --stage m5` also accepts `--raid <name>` and `--blind`.
- `m5/raids.json` is `{theme, public, blind}`: a theme string and two ordered arrays of base names. The heist theme uses separate public and blind lists. Automatic selection skips names already present in `m5/raids_used.jsonl`; after the base names it cycles through the same list with suffixes `2`, `3`, etc. Explicit names are recorded too.
- Each ledger row and `C/raid.json` has exactly `{raid, blind, run_root, utc}`; `run_root` is absolute and `utc` is an ISO UTC timestamp. Reservations are serialised. A run reuses its existing reservation and rejects conflicting raid/blind arguments. The launcher reserves against the original pipeline ledger before freezing its copy.
- m5 sets `args.chat_prefix = "x-<raid>"`. Other scripts opt in using `args.chat_prefix`, an agent option `chat_prefix`, or the workflow flag `--chat-prefix`. Without a prefix, runner naming stays unchanged.
- Names are `<chat_prefix>-<label>[-<descriptor>]`; labels are lowercased, non-`[a-z0-9-]` runs become `-`, edge hyphens are removed, and an empty label becomes `agent`. Concurrent sibling calls sharing a label within a stage add `1of<n>`, `2of<n>`, etc. Repair turns add `retry<k>` (starting at 1); fallback calls add `fb`. When needed together, descriptors appear in that order, separated by hyphens. Harness repair calls supply agent option `retry: 1`.
- wf passes the name to every runner as `name`. OpenCode uses `--title`, Claude uses `--name`, and Codex prepends `[<name>]` as the first prompt line, before role instructions.

content.content: 230	- wf's optional agent setting `isolation` has `{directory, hidden, box_access}`: an absolute private view directory, an array of absolute paths hidden from that role, and a boolean permitting box credentials. It overrides cwd and add-dirs, disables resume-cache reuse and provider-session export, and is forwarded to every dispatched family, including fallbacks. Real dispatch uses bubblewrap with a read-only host filesystem, private `/tmp`, PID/IPC namespaces, hidden run/workflow paths and provider histories, and a fresh writable HOME containing authentication files only. The view is the only writable host directory. The initial implementer additionally receives read-only access to the existing box wrapper and SSH keys. Test, review and repair roles cannot access them. No sandbox fallback grants broader access: missing bubblewrap or unavailable namespaces fails the call. That outer namespace is the only sandbox: hosts that restrict unprivileged user namespaces (Ubuntu's AppArmor `bwrap-userns-restrict`) deny any namespace nested inside it, so a provider's own sandbox would fail every command. Inside the namespace a Codex agent therefore runs with `danger-full-access`, never `workspace-write` or `read-only`. That mode follows only from the call being dispatched inside the namespace, never from an environment variable: a Codex call outside isolation keeps `workspace-write` or `read-only` even when `CODEX_EPHEMERAL=1` is set. A role whose tools include Write, Edit or Bash keeps the view writable; any other role gets the view mounted read-only, with only its private HOME and temporary directory writable. `WF_STUB` remains an explicit test double, bypassing provider execution. Temporary views/provider state are removed after the stage; raw provider logs remain under the role's workflow transcript directory and are hidden from other roles.

## Sealed comparison (U57, U58) - Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 to s17. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs, or from a published evaluator that the pipeline runs on each arm's output without naming the arm. Criteria, margins, thresholds, reference values and timeouts are fixed by a science step before the run, sealed, and unreadable by the run's agents. Compute is recorded twice and never mixed: per invocation as attribution (the arm's own subprocesses only) and per box allocation as the bill. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run; a design whose launch depends on an earlier run's outcomes is launched only when the science step finds them in that run's `C/comparison_scored.json`. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged. - Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup, order_seed, timeout_s, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, bootstrap_resamples, comparisons}`: - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what, commands, env}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual. - `commands`: null, or 1 to 8 commands, each a non-empty array of non-empty strings: the exact published command lines of the arm, in order, as argument vectors run without a shell. When non-null, the pipeline runs them itself (see Evaluate) and the arm's adapter only prepares. - `env`: null or an object mapping names that match `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` and do not start with `CMP_` to strings; set for the arm's commands. - Placeholders, in command and `env` strings only: `{input}` (the input id), `{run}`, `{out}` (the absolute paths of the invocation's `run/` and `out/`) and `{spec:

}` with `

` a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the input's `spec`, which must resolve in every input's `spec` to a string (inserted as is) or a finite number (inserted as `json.dumps` writes it). `{{` and `}}` stand for literal braces; any other `{` or `}` makes the design invalid. Substitution replaces every occurrence and is not repeated on its result. - `inputs`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{id, spec}`: `id` a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; `spec` any JSON value (pins, case, configuration). - `outputs`: 0 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, what, format, select}`: a logical result each arm, or the evaluator, writes for an input, compared across arms. `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `what` a non-empty string; `format` `"bytes"`, `"text_numbers"` (every number in the file's UTF-8 text, in order, as matched by `[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?` together with `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` tokens) or `"json_numbers"` (every number leaf of the JSON document, in document order; booleans are not numbers). `select` is null (the whole content) or, for `bytes` and `text_numbers` only, a Python `re` pattern with at least one capturing group: the content is read as UTF-8 with replacement, and the selected content is every group of every match of `re.finditer(select, text, re.MULTILINE)`, in order (an unmatched group as the empty string), joined by `"\n"`; `format` then applies to the selected content (`bytes` to its UTF-8 encoding). Several outputs may select different parts of the same file, each with its own comparison and tolerance. - `metrics`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, unit, what, source, scope, reduce, expect_count}`: `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `unit` and `what` non-empty strings; `source` `"trusted_wall"` or `"sealed_extraction"`. - `trusted_wall`: `scope` `"commands"` (the summed wall seconds of the arm's commands; every arm must have non-null `commands`), `"invocation"` (the adapter's wall plus its commands' walls) or `"invocation_and_evaluator"` (that plus the evaluator's wall; needs a non-null `evaluator`). `reduce` and `expect_count` are null. - `sealed_extraction`: read from fetched files by a rule the harness agent fixes before the run, reduced as the design states. `scope` null; `reduce` `"last"`, `"first"`, `"min"`, `"max"`, `"mean"`, `"value_at_max_key"` or `"value_at_min_key"`; `expect_count` null or a positive integer, the number of matched values the rule must find. - `evaluator`: null or exactly `{what, spec, timeout_s}`: a published, pinned program that reads one arm's output for one input, with data that only it may read, and writes evaluation files. `what` a non-empty string; `spec` any JSON value (program, pin, command, and where its private data come from); `timeout_s` null or a positive integer. - `replicates` an integer from 1 to 30; `warmup` an integer from 0 to 3; `order_seed` and `bootstrap_seed` integers; `bootstrap_resamples` an integer from 1000 to 1000000; `budget_s` a positive integer, the evaluate stage's time budget for this comparison. When `args.run_ceiling_s` is present, `budget_s` must be below it. - `timeout_s`: null, a positive integer for every invocation, or an object mapping every arm id to a positive integer or to an object mapping every input id to a positive integer: the cap of one invocation's arm part. - `comparisons`: 1 to 12 items, each exactly `{id, arm, against, measure, criterion, direction, unit, pairing, rule, confidence, margin, threshold, strict, reference, missing, given, parts}`: - `id` unique, matching `^K[0-9]{1,2}$`; `arm` an arm id; `against` a different arm id or `"reference"`; `parts` a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings. - `measure` is exactly `{metric}` (a metric name) or exactly `{output, comparator}` (an output name and one of `"exact"`, `"elementwise_abs"`, `"elementwise_rel"`, `"elementwise_abs_plus_rel"`, `"elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max"`). An output comparison needs an arm as `against`. - `criterion` `"equivalence"`, `"non_inferiority"`, `"superiority"`, `"ratio_at_least"` or `"agreement"`. `agreement` is the criterion of every output comparison and of no metric comparison. - `direction` `"higher_better"`, `"lower_better"` or `"two_sided"`: the metric as measured (for wall seconds, `lower_better`). `equivalence` and `agreement` use `two_sided`; `non_inferiority` and `ratio_at_least` use `higher_better` or `lower_better`; `superiority` takes any. - `unit` `"pooled_mean"` (each replicate's value is the mean over inputs, decided once), `"per_input_all"` (decided per input; the comparison holds only if it holds on every input) or `"per_input_each"` (decided and reported per input). `ratio_at_least` uses `pooled_mean`. - `pairing` `"paired_replicate"` or `"unpaired"`; output comparisons use `paired_replicate`. - `rule` `"all_pairs"` or `"bootstrap"`; `confidence` a number in `[0.5, 1)` for `bootstrap` and null for `all_pairs`. Output comparisons use `all_pairs`. - `margin`: null, `{"abs": x}`, `{"rel": y}` or `{"abs": x, "rel": y}` with `x` and `y` finite and nonnegative. For an output comparison it is the comparator's tolerance: `elementwise_abs` needs `abs`, `elementwise_rel` needs `rel`, `elementwise_abs_plus_rel` and `elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max` need both, `exact` needs null. For a metric comparison it is null, `abs` or `rel`; `rel` scales by `abs(reference)` against a reference, else by `abs(mean of the against arm's values)` for the same unit. - `threshold`: a finite number above 0 for `ratio_at_least`, otherwise null. `strict`: a boolean for `ratio_at_least` (true: the bound must exceed `threshold`; false: it may equal it), otherwise null. - `reference`: exactly when `against` is `"reference"`, an object `{source, values}`: `source` a non-empty string naming where the values come from (for example an earlier run of this route and the rule that derived them), `values` mapping every input id to a finite number; otherwise null. - `missing`: `"drop"`, `"void"` or `"fail"`, how a missing value is decided (see Scoring). `agreement` uses `void` or `fail`. - `given`: an array, possibly empty, of unique ids of comparisons that come earlier in `comparisons`; a decision unit is decided only when each of them is supported for it (see Scoring). An invalid argument or design, or a path that cannot be read as JSON, fails intake with `error_class: parse` before any agent call. - Before the intake agent call and any box command, the pipeline writes atomically, in this order: `C/comparison.json`, exactly `{source, source_sha256, design}`; `C/comparison_seal.json`, exactly `{comparison_sha256, sealed_utc}` (the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of `C/comparison.json`); and `A/comparison_view.json`, exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup}` copied from the design, with `evaluator` reduced to `{what, spec}` (null when the design's is null). The view holds no comparison, criterion, margin, threshold, reference value, timeout, part, seed or budget. Agents see only the view; comparison-mode prompts name it and never `C/` or the design path. The science step that writes the design is responsible for the view's free text (`what`, `spec`, `select`) stating no expectation, criterion or result. - Isolation, comparison mode only: every agent call of the run (intake, harness, and every setup and anchors repair) is dispatched with wf `isolation` (see Implement), `box_access` false, and `hidden` containing at least the run's absolute `C/` directory and the design's absolute path. A call that cannot be dispatched so fails as an isolation failure does; there is no fallback. Agents therefore cannot read criteria, margins, thresholds, references or timeouts from files, not only from prompts. - Intake prompt, comparison mode only: the run compares the view's arms on the view's inputs; `A0` is the benchmark intake records as usual; intake also records, in `benchmark.json` under the key `arms`, each other arm's published source, pin and commands, under the key `evaluator` the evaluator's published source, pin and command when the view has one, and in `data.json` every input any arm or the evaluator needs, marking the evaluator's private data. - Harness prompt, comparison mode only: `setup.sh` also builds or installs every arm's published program and configuration, and the evaluator, as published. `setup.sh` places every file only the evaluator may read under the top-level directory `cmp-private/` of the shared run directory and nowhere else. The harness agent writes, besides the usual scripts: - one adapter `harness/arms/.sh` per arm, `A0` included. For an arm with `commands`, the adapter only prepares the invocation (stages the input named by `CMP_INPUT` under `run/` or `CMP_OUT`) and does not run the arm's program; the pipeline runs the commands. For an arm without `commands`, the adapter runs that arm's published program and configuration on that input and writes its results under `CMP_OUT`. Adapters never write or patch source, never compute, write or assert a metric, and never name `cmp-private` or `CMP_PRIVATE`; - when the view has an evaluator, `harness/evaluate.sh`, which runs the published, pinned evaluator on the arm output in `CMP_ARM_OUT` for the input named by `CMP_INPUT`, reads private data only under `CMP_PRIVATE`, writes its results under `CMP_EVAL_OUT`, and never writes under `CMP_ARM_OUT`; - `harness/cmp_files.json`, exactly `{"files": {...}}`, mapping each arm id to an object that maps every output name to a location: a relative path, or exactly `{glob, order}` with `glob` a pattern of relative-path components that may also use `*`, `?`, `[` and `]`, and `order` `"lexical"` or `"natural"`. Locations are relative to the invocation directory, and their first component is `out` (the arm's files) or `eval` (the evaluator's files); - `harness/cmp_extract.json`, exactly `{"rules": [...]}`, one rule per arm and `sealed_extraction` metric, each exactly `{arm, metric, file, kind, expr}`, with `file` a relative path whose first component is `out` or `eval`, and `kind` and `expr` as defined for `harness/card_extract.json` (U54), extended by the metric's `reduce`: `kind` `"json"`: `expr` points to a finite number, to an array of finite numbers, or (for `value_at_max_key` and `value_at_min_key`) to an array of two-element arrays `[key, value]` of finite numbers; `kind` `"regex"`: exactly one capturing group, or exactly two (key, then value) for `value_at_max_key` and `value_at_min_key`; - `harness/versions.sh`, which prints one JSON object mapping each arm id, and `"evaluator"` when the view has one, to exactly `{version, executable}`: the program's version string and the path, absolute or relative to the shared run directory, of its main executable file. Relative paths are one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none `.` or `..`. `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` keep their meaning for `A0`. - After harness generation or copy (with `args.harness_from`, the source directory must also hold `arms/`, `cmp_files.json`, `cmp_extract.json`, `versions.sh` and, when the design has an evaluator, `evaluate.sh`, copied like the scripts) and before the harness upload, those files must exist and be valid: `harness/arms/` holds exactly one non-empty adapter per arm; `evaluate.sh` exists exactly when the design has an evaluator; `cmp_files.json` maps every arm and every output, with `eval` locations only when the design has an evaluator; `cmp_extract.json` has exactly one rule per arm and `sealed_extraction` metric, whose group count matches the metric's `reduce`; and no adapter's bytes contain `cmp-private` or `CMP_PRIVATE`. Otherwise reproduce fails with `error_class: parse` before the upload. The pipeline then writes `C/arms_seal.json`, exactly `{files, sealed_utc}`, mapping each of those files' names (adapters as `arms/.sh`) to the SHA-256 of its bytes. They upload with the harness, in the same encoding. No repair changes them. - In comparison mode reproduce runs exactly as usual for `A0`. Profile, seal, propose and implement are SKIPPED. Evaluate runs the comparison when reproduce passed, and is SKIPPED otherwise, as after any failed gate. - Evaluate, comparison mode (U57): - Versions: one box command, operation `versions`, runs `bash harness/versions.sh` with stdout to `out/comparison/versions.json`, then the trusted `python3 profiler/cmp_system.py` (written inline by the pipeline) writes `out/comparison/system.json`, exactly `{cpu_model, cpu_logical, kernel, driver_version, cuda_version, gpus, executables}`: `lscpu` model name and logical CPU count; `uname -r`; the driver and CUDA versions that `nvidia-smi` reports; `gpus` one row per GPU, exactly `{index, name, uuid, memory_total}`, from `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,uuid,memory.total --format=csv,noheader`; and `executables` mapping each key of `versions.json` to exactly `{version, executable, sha256, libraries}`, with `sha256` the SHA-256 of the executable's resolved file and `libraries` one row per `ldd` line of the form ` => ...`, exactly `{name, path, sha256}` (the resolved file's SHA-256), or `[]` when `ldd` fails or reports a static executable. Any field that cannot be read is null. - Rounds: `warmup` warmup rounds, then `replicates` replicate rounds. Each round runs every (arm, input) pair once, in an order drawn from one `random.Random(order_seed)` stream: one `shuffle` of the round's pairs per round, warmups included. - Each invocation is one box command, operation `comparison`, from the shared run directory. It builds a fresh invocation directory `comparison-work/ or r>///` holding `run/` (a symbolic link to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work`, `evaluation-work`, `units-check`, `comparison-work` and `cmp-private`), an empty `out/` and an empty `eval/`, then runs the trusted wrapper `python3 profiler/cmp_wrap.py` (written inline by the pipeline, as the profile stage writes its probe). The wrapper: 1. sets the mode of `cmp-private`, when it exists, to `000`; 2. arm part: runs `bash harness/arms/.sh` with working directory `run/`; then, when the adapter exits 0 and the arm has `commands`, runs each command in order with working directory `run/`, after placeholder substitution, with its standard output and error written to `out/cmd.stdout` and `out/cmd.stderr` (`k` from 1), stopping at the first nonzero exit. A first argument containing `/` resolves relative to `run/`, otherwise through `PATH`. The arm's `env` applies to its commands; 3. restores the mode of `cmp-private` to `700`; when the mode was not `000` just before the restore, the invocation is `invalid`; 4. evaluator part, only when the design has an evaluator and the arm part's status is `ok`: runs `bash harness/evaluate.sh` with working directory `run/`; 5. writes `wrap.json` in the invocation directory, atomically and last, exactly `{status, adapter_rc, adapter_wall_s, commands, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_status, eval_rc, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, eval_gpu_busy_known}`. `status` is `"ok"` (the adapter and every command exited 0), `"failed"` (a nonzero exit), `"timeout"` or `"invalid"`; `commands` has one row per command started, exactly `{argv, rc, wall_s, executable, sha256}` (the substituted argument vector, exit status, `perf_counter` wall seconds, the resolved executable path and its SHA-256, null when unresolved); `eval_status` is `"ok"`, `"failed"`, `"timeout"` or `"skipped"` (no evaluator, or the arm part was not `ok`). Walls are `perf_counter` seconds and exit statuses null on timeout. GPU-busy seconds are sampled separately for the arm part and the evaluator part (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu` immediately and every second; each finite sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100` seconds, summed over GPUs; the matching `known` flag is false when no valid sample was taken). The environment of the adapter and the commands carries `CMP_ARM`, `CMP_INPUT` (the input id), `CMP_INPUT_SPEC` (the JSON of that input's `spec`), `CMP_MODE` (`warmup` or `replicate`), `CMP_ROUND` (the index) and `CMP_OUT` (the absolute path of `out/`). The evaluator's environment carries `CMP_INPUT`, `CMP_INPUT_SPEC`, `CMP_MODE`, `CMP_ROUND`, `CMP_ARM_OUT` (the absolute path of `out/`), `CMP_EVAL_OUT` (the absolute path of `eval/`) and `CMP_PRIVATE` (the absolute path of `cmp-private`), and never the arm id. The invocation's `out/`, `eval/` and `wrap.json` are fetched to `A/results/evaluate/comparison/ or r>///`. - Timeouts: the arm part's timeout is the smallest of its `timeout_s` (when non-null), the time left in `budget_s`, and the time left before the run ceiling; the evaluator part's is the smallest of `evaluator.timeout_s` (when non-null) and the same two. On a timeout the wrapper kills the part's whole process group and records `"timeout"`. When the time left in `budget_s` is below 1 s, the remaining invocations are not run, and their status is `"not_run"`. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` gives status `"invalid"`. - Values: for an invocation with status `ok`, a `trusted_wall` metric is, by `scope`, the sum of its commands' `wall_s` (`commands`), `adapter_wall_s` plus that sum (`invocation`), or that plus `eval_wall_s` (`invocation_and_evaluator`, null unless `eval_status` is `ok`). A `sealed_extraction` metric is its rule applied to the fetched file: the matched values are every `float()`-parsed match of the regex in order, or the number or array at the pointer. With `reduce` `last`, `first`, `min`, `max` or `mean`, the value is that function of the matched values; with `value_at_max_key` or `value_at_min_key`, it is the value of the first pair whose key is the largest or smallest. A file under `eval` needs `eval_status` `ok`. A missing or unreadable file, no match, a nonfinite matched number, or a match count other than a non-null `expect_count` gives null. Every value of an invocation with any other status is null. A null value is a missing value. - Compute (G6): `A/results/evaluate/comparison_compute.json`, written atomically after the last invocation, is exactly `{invocations, arms, all_invocations, system, versions, allocation}`. - `invocations` has one row per scheduled invocation in run order, each exactly `{round, arm, input, status, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_status, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, attributed_usd}`, from `wrap.json`: `wall_s` is `adapter_wall_s` plus the commands' walls, and `attributed_usd` is `(wall_s + eval_wall_s) / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h`, with a null wall counted as 0 and null when the price is unavailable. Rows of `not_run` invocations have null numbers. - `arms` has one row per arm, each exactly `{arm, invocations, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over that arm's replicate invocations whatever their status; `gpu_busy_known` is true only when every summed row's flag is. - `all_invocations` is exactly `{invocations, wall_s, eval_wall_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over every row, warmups and failures included. - `system` and `versions` copy the fetched `system.json` and `versions.json` (null when missing or invalid). - `allocation` is the bill of the whole box allocation, which may include work outside this run, exactly `{type, price_usd_h, started_utc, ended_utc, hours, usd, final}` from `C/box.json`. When that record has `ended_utc` and `hours`, they are copied and `final` is true; otherwise `ended_utc` is null, `hours` is the time from `started_utc` to when the file is written, and `final` is false. `usd` is `hours * price_usd_h`. Unavailable fields are null. At takeaways, after a matching allocation record refreshes `C/box.json` (see Compute metadata), the pipeline rewrites the file atomically with only `allocation` recomputed. The run's own share stays `run_box_usd`. Uploads, links and fetches are outside every invocation row; they remain in the stage's receipts. - Scoring (U58): after the last invocation, `python3 -I m5/score_comparison.py `. It checks the SHA-256 of `C/comparison.json` against `C/comparison_seal.json` and of each sealed harness file against `C/arms_seal.json`, then scores each comparison, in design order, from the replicate rounds only. - Locations: a relative path names one file. A `{glob, order}` location names the regular files that Python `glob.glob(glob, root_dir=)` returns, sorted by their relative path (`lexical`), or by a key that splits the relative path into runs of digits and non-digits, compares digit runs as integers and breaks ties by the path (`natural`); their contents, each after `select`, are joined by `"\n"` (by `b"\n"` for `bytes`). A side of an (input, replicate) pair is missing when its invocation's status is not `ok`, when the location is under `eval` and `eval_status` is not `ok`, when the location names no file or an unreadable one, when the content cannot be parsed as the output's `format`, or when the selected content is empty (no bytes for `bytes`, no numbers otherwise). - Output comparisons (`agreement`): for each input and replicate where neither side is missing, the comparator compares the two contents. `exact`: identical bytes. Otherwise both contents are parsed as the output's `format` into number lists; different lengths, or a NaN in one list but not at the same position in the other, disagree; equal infinities agree; finite pairs agree when `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol` (`elementwise_abs`), `abs(a - b) <= rel_tol * abs(b)` (`elementwise_rel`, `b` the `against` arm's element), `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * abs(b)` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel`) or `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * max(abs(a), abs(b))` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`). A pair agrees when every element agrees. Each compared pair records `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error` over its finite elements (null when none). - Metric comparisons: an arm's value for (replicate, input) is the metric value above. For `pooled_mean`, a replicate's value is the mean over inputs, null when any input's value is null. The statistics are, per decision unit (the pooled value, or each input), over the replicates where the values they need are present: for `paired_replicate`, the difference `arm - against` per replicate where both have values (or `arm - reference value`); for `unpaired`, the differences of every arm value with every against value (or with the reference value). `ratio_at_least` uses the ratio of means `mean(arm) / mean(against)` for `higher_better` and `mean(against) / mean(arm)` for `lower_better`, over the replicates where both have values. For `pooled_mean` against a reference, the reference value is the mean of `values` over inputs. - Missing values, per decision unit: `n_missing` counts the arm's missing values and, against an arm, the against arm's (for `pooled_mean` a replicate counts once; for agreement a pair with a missing side counts once). With `missing` `"drop"`, they are left out as above. With `"void"`, any missing value makes the unit void with reason `"missing_values"`. With `"fail"`, a missing value of `arm` makes the unit `"not_supported"` with reason `"missing_values"`, and otherwise a missing value of `against` makes it void with reason `"missing_values"`. - Eligibility (`given`): before anything else, for each listed comparison, its outcome for this unit is that comparison's row for the same input when both comparisons are decided per input, and otherwise that comparison's outcome, where `"per_input"` counts as supported only when every row is. When any of these is not `"supported"`, the unit is void with reason `"not_eligible"`. - Interval: for `all_pairs`, `[lo, hi]` is the minimum and maximum of the differences (for a ratio, of the per-replicate ratios in the same orientation), and needs at least one difference. For `bootstrap`, the statistic (the mean difference, or the ratio of means) is recomputed on `bootstrap_resamples` resamples (`B`) with replacement of the unit's paired replicates (for `unpaired`, of each arm's values separately), drawn from one `random.Random(bootstrap_seed)` stream in comparison order, and `[lo, hi]` is the `(1 - confidence) / 2` and `(1 + confidence) / 2` empirical quantiles (sorted resamples, index `floor(q * (B - 1))`); it needs at least two replicates. `estimate` is the statistic on the full data. Too few values gives outcome `"void"` with reason `"insufficient_replicates"`; no values at all gives reason `"missing_values"`. - Margin value `m`: 0 for a null margin, `x` for `{"abs": x}`, and for `{"rel": y}` `y * abs(reference value)` or `y * abs(mean of the against arm's values in the unit)`. - Outcome per decision unit, in this order: eligibility, then the missing-value rule, then the interval's minimum count, then the criterion. The criterion gives `"supported"`, `"not_supported"` or else `"inconclusive"`: agreement is supported when at least one pair was compared, every compared pair agrees and none is missing, and not supported when any compared pair disagrees (with no compared pair and no missing side, it is void with reason `"missing_values"`); equivalence is supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`, not supported when `hi < -m` or `lo > m`; non-inferiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo >= -m`, not supported when `hi < -m`; non-inferiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi <= m`, not supported when `lo > m`; superiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo > m`, not supported when `hi <= m`; superiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi < -m`, not supported when `lo >= -m`; superiority (`two_sided`) is supported when `lo > m` or `hi < -m`, not supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`; ratio with `strict` false is supported when `lo >= threshold`, not supported when `hi < threshold`; ratio with `strict` true is supported when `lo > threshold`, not supported when `hi <= threshold`. - `sign` of a unit is `"higher"` when a `two_sided` superiority is supported with `lo > m`, `"lower"` when it is supported with `hi < -m`, and null otherwise. - A comparison's outcome: for `pooled_mean`, its one unit's outcome; for `per_input_all`, supported when every input is supported, not supported when any input is not supported, void when any input is void and none is not supported, otherwise inconclusive; for `per_input_each`, `"per_input"`, with each input's outcome in its rows. - `C/comparison_scored.json`, atomic, is exactly `{comparison_sha256, comparisons, totals}`. `comparisons` follows the design's order, each exactly `{id, arm, against, criterion, unit, outcome, rows}`; `rows` has one row per decision unit (`input` null for `pooled_mean`), each exactly `{input, n, n_missing, estimate, lo, hi, margin_value, threshold, outcome, sign, reason, pairs}`. `n` counts the differences, ratios or compared pairs; `pairs` is null for metric comparisons and, for agreement, the per-replicate rows `{replicate, agrees, missing, max_abs_error, max_rel_error}` (`agrees` null and `missing` true when a side is missing). Numbers are null when void; `reason` is `"missing_values"`, `"insufficient_replicates"` or `"not_eligible"` for a void unit, `"missing_values"` for a unit made not supported by the `"fail"` rule, and null otherwise. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons. - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` or fetched file is not invalid input; it is a missing value. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`. - Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode, and add optional `comparisons_total`, `comparisons_supported`, `comparisons_not_supported`, `comparisons_inconclusive` and `comparisons_void` (decision units, nonnegative integers), all null outside comparison mode, on SKIPPED/stub records and whenever the scored file was not written; records without them stay valid.

## Sealed comparison (U57, U58) - Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 to s17. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs, or from a published evaluator that the pipeline runs on each arm's output without naming the arm. Criteria, margins, thresholds, reference values and timeouts are fixed by a science step before the run, sealed, and unreadable by the run's agents. Compute is recorded twice and never mixed: per invocation as attribution (the arm's own subprocesses only) and per box allocation as the bill. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run; a design whose launch depends on an earlier run's outcomes is launched only when the science step finds them in that run's `C/comparison_scored.json`. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged. - Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup, order_seed, timeout_s, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, bootstrap_resamples, comparisons}`: - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what, commands, env}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual. - `commands`: null, or 1 to 8 commands, each a non-empty array of non-empty strings: the exact published command lines of the arm, in order, as argument vectors run without a shell. }` with `

` a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the input's `spec`, which must resolve in every input's `spec` to a string (inserted as is) or a finite number (inserted as `json.dumps` writes it). `{{` and `}}` stand for literal braces; any other `{` or `}` makes the design invalid. Several outputs may select different parts of the same file, each with its own comparison and tolerance. - `metrics`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, unit, what, source, scope, reduce, expect_count}`: `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `unit` and `what` non-empty strings; `source` `"trusted_wall"` or `"sealed_extraction"`. - `trusted_wall`: `scope` `"commands"` (the summed wall seconds of the arm's commands; every arm must have non-null `commands`), `"invocation"` (the adapter's wall plus its commands' walls) or `"invocation_and_evaluator"` (that plus the evaluator's wall; needs a non-null `evaluator`). `reduce` and `expect_count` are null. - `sealed_extraction`: read from fetched files by a rule the harness agent fixes before the run, reduced as the design states. `scope` null; `reduce` `"last"`, `"first"`, `"min"`, `"max"`, `"mean"`, `"value_at_max_key"` or `"value_at_min_key"`; `expect_count` null or a positive integer, the number of matched values the rule must find. - `evaluator`: null or exactly `{what, spec, timeout_s}`: a published, pinned program that reads one arm's output for one input, with data that only it may read, and writes evaluation files. `what` a non-empty string; `spec` any JSON value (program, pin, command, and where its private data come from); `timeout_s` null or a positive integer. - `replicates` an integer from 1 to 30; `warmup` an integer from 0 to 3; `order_seed` and `bootstrap_seed` integers; `bootstrap_resamples` an integer from 1000 to 1000000; `budget_s` a positive integer, the evaluate stage's time budget for this comparison. An output comparison needs an arm as `against`. - `criterion` `"equivalence"`, `"non_inferiority"`, `"superiority"`, `"ratio_at_least"` or `"agreement"`. `agreement` is the criterion of every output comparison and of no metric comparison. - `direction` `"higher_better"`, `"lower_better"` or `"two_sided"`: the metric as measured (for wall seconds, `lower_better`). `equivalence` and `agreement` use `two_sided`; `non_inferiority` and `ratio_at_least` use `higher_better` or `lower_better`; `superiority` takes any. - `unit` `"pooled_mean"` (each replicate's value is the mean over inputs, decided once), `"per_input_all"` (decided per input; the comparison holds only if it holds on every input) or `"per_input_each"` (decided and reported per input). `ratio_at_least` uses `pooled_mean`. - `pairing` `"paired_replicate"` or `"unpaired"`; output comparisons use `paired_replicate`. - `rule` `"all_pairs"` or `"bootstrap"`; `confidence` a number in `[0.5, 1)` for `bootstrap` and null for `all_pairs`. Output comparisons use `all_pairs`. - `margin`: null, `{"abs": x}`, `{"rel": y}` or `{"abs": x, "rel": y}` with `x` and `y` finite and nonnegative. For an output comparison it is the comparator's tolerance: `elementwise_abs` needs `abs`, `elementwise_rel` needs `rel`, `elementwise_abs_plus_rel` and `elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max` need both, `exact` needs null. For a metric comparison it is null, `abs` or `rel`; `rel` scales by `abs(reference)` against a reference, else by `abs(mean of the against arm's values)` for the same unit. - `threshold`: a finite number above 0 for `ratio_at_least`, otherwise null. `strict`: a boolean for `ratio_at_least` (true: the bound must exceed `threshold`; false: it may equal it), otherwise null. - `reference`: exactly when `against` is `"reference"`, an object `{source, values}`: `source` a non-empty string naming where the values come from (for example an earlier run of this route and the rule that derived them), `values` mapping every input id to a finite number; otherwise null. - `missing`: `"drop"`, `"void"` or `"fail"`, how a missing value is decided (see Scoring). `agreement` uses `void` or `fail`. - `given`: an array, possibly empty, of unique ids of comparisons that come earlier in `comparisons`; a decision unit is decided only when each of them is supported for it (see Scoring). Numbers are null when void; `reason` is `"missing_values"`, `"insufficient_replicates"` or `"not_eligible"` for a void unit, `"missing_values"` for a unit made not supported by the `"fail"` rule, and null otherwise. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons. - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` or fetched file is not invalid input; it is a missing value. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`. - Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode, and add optional `comparisons_total`, `comparisons_supported`, `comparisons_not_supported`, `comparisons_inconclusive` and `comparisons_void` (decision units, nonnegative integers), all null outside comparison mode, on SKIPPED/stub records and whenever the scored file was not written; records without them stay valid.
